title: Draft: Conditional κ = 7.10436534421701e-4: concave-descent frame retiming of 25 gates on #251's source527 banks
body:
Conditional κ = `710436534421701/10^18` = **7.10436534421701e-4**, +2.85 × 10⁻⁹ over [#251](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/251) (7.10433687047883e-4). Stacked on #251's unmerged 37-entrance construction at `2b030c0`.

**Status: draft, not a leaderboard candidate.** This is above #251, #252 and #253, but below the #254 lineage; #258 independently composes the same 25-gate retiming with #254, and #259 (518 entrances, 7.11029e-4) is now far ahead. This PR stays as the Python-verifier (eight-stage `verify.py`) form of the retiming on #251's word.

**Full replay: PASS.** `verify.py --output /tmp/descent-source527-verification` completed all eight mandatory stages with package integrity unchanged in 347 s: `{"status": "PASS_IMMUTABLE_PARITY_REGAUGED_DESCENT_SOURCE527_FIVE_STAGE_BANKED_CONSTRUCTION", "manifest_sha256": "00119cd179dcc2c837c0c9bf53f32f5131a9c88e278f7aad41e84179be5e2a42", "files": 133, "kappa": "710436534421701/1000000000000000000", "fresh_stages": ["banks", "bit", "complex", "finite", "math", "primes", "raw", "scalar"], "inputs_unchanged": true}`.

## Change

A second exact frame retiming of #251's regauged source527 ADD word. Twenty-five internal `forward_gate` ADD frames (25 of 786,623 gates) are reassigned by local descent on the concave paid-rank objective Σ r·ln(120/r), using only frames already present on the operands' chains. The local paid histogram changes by {2: −2, 4: +24, 5: −48, 6: +25, 11: −1, 13: +2, 17: −1}: one local recursive call per helper invocation disappears at unchanged rank mass 433,953. The literal construction keeps 24 replicas, stock 521,425 and deficit 105,600 with 11,792,160 paid calls (was 11,792,280); the per-replica bank call count is 491,340 (was 491,345). Banks, charts, entrances, prime witnesses, the scalar word and every endpoint are unchanged.

Why this is the whole retiming budget: for the window (prev, cur, next) of a register the objective is concave in dim(cur), so each gate is optimal at either the minimal frame (join of the operands' previous frames and their source spans) or the maximal frame (meet of the next frames). On #251's word 99.7 % of gates have those two coincide with the current frame; the fully eager (greatest-fixpoint) assignment is worse (Σ r·ln(120/r) = 1.1817 × 10⁶ vs 1.1374 × 10⁶), and block moves (raising or lowering whole runs between ascents) are blocked by partner chains or source spans. The 25 gates are what remains.

## Verification

`descent_transform.py` consumes the frozen `descent-selection.json` (record bindings, old basis hashes, explicit rational new bases) and, like PR244's `retiming_transform.py`, rebuilds every MOVE from the selected gate needs and independently checks: nested chains, fixed source/dirty/target endpoints, nondegenerate endpoint bases, both reflected annihilator ledgers, unchanged COPY lifetimes, the byte-identical scalar/COPY projection, and the expected histogram delta and rank mass. In addition it recomputes the exact **integer** source span of every non-target operand from the actual scalar word and requires it inside the new frame (the inherited word satisfies this invariant for all 1.57 M non-target operand instances; targets live in cap coordinates and are excluded, as in the inherited word). `raw_ledger.rebind_descent` recounts the five-stage profile (493,656 calls, rank mass 2,830,840, deficit 4,400); `bank_check` and `verify.py` require the new counts and κ.

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/five-stage-source527-banks/requirements.txt
python3 -B research/five-stage-source527-banks/verify.py --output /tmp/descent-source527-verification
```

Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.14.0, a new output directory outside the package; no network.

Before this PR was opened, the new transform stage passed inside the full verifier (`PASS concave descent retiming 25 gates 95452 paid calls 885276 records`) and the κ was reproduced with the package's own moment/outer engines (`710436534421701/10^18`); the complete eight-stage replay with the final package is in progress.

## Scope and credits

Exactly #251's hypotheses and conditional interfaces (all-size compiler, weighted chart, restored rows, selectors, routing, prime supply, precision/recovery, complex symbolic correctness, analytic reduction). No new Lean build or practical benchmark is claimed.

eumemic (#251, #249, #244, #210): the source527 construction, entrance transport, common-frame retiming and verifier; hcg890 and Jacob Sussman (#234); Evan McKinney (#197); Chafik Boukhalfa (#200); Avi Eisenberg (#193); Dugongue (#216), sennemmi (#230) and the retained PR207/211/237 lineage. The concave-descent retiming and this package's rebinding were prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance.

title: Fixed-prime refinement of PR259 (kappa = 0.000711029389987426878345881)
body:
**Research closeout — Draft retained; no current-record claim.** This is an exact fixed-prime arithmetic refinement of [PR #259](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/259). It inherits #259's finite physical construction and changes the conditional bit-supplier calculation only.

## Result and contribution boundary

```text
PR #259: 142205877210807 / 200000000000000000
PR #261: 711029389987426878345881 / 10^27
Exact gain: 3933391878345881 / 10^27
```

At `m = 120`, the certificate fixes `q = 2^127 - 1`, uses rare-class density `rho = 3456000/q < 10^-16`, and charges the complete `32m^2` rare-child fallback. It retains #259's 518 pivot entrances, four cuts, physical frames, routes, roles, replicas and lifetimes unchanged. It makes no new physical-DAG saving.

The finite arithmetic replay regenerates the cohort profile and invoice, uses two rational interval engines for the coarse endpoint, checks eight finite levels, 47 strict outer constraints and seven margins, and rejects the adjacent `10^-27` grid point. The fresh finite coefficient is `62639910650427201 < 2^80 < q`; selector, chart, normalizer, signed-prefix and inherited physical costs remain charged.

**Attribution:** Dugongue's #259 provides the inherited multi-cut physical witness and invoice; its pinned source lineage comes from #249. The fixed-prime approach credits Nespoli #235 and Arun #252, with #255/#258 refinements acknowledged in the certificate history. The exact recomputation, certificate, documentation and workflow integration in this PR were prepared by sennemmi with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Upstream authorship, source notices and license files are retained; the added package carries its stated Apache-2.0 license.

## Incremental review path

The full PR comparison against `main` is large because it carries the upstream research lineage: GitHub reports 422 changed files and 1,707,820 additions. Removing inherited source or receipts would weaken provenance or replayability, so this closeout keeps them intact. The independently reviewable increment is exactly one commit over #259 SHA `a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c` at head `d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef`: [compare #259 to #261](https://github.com/sennemmi/integer-mult-bounds/compare/a53ec0ca4d59634f16630dd16adf035c9f12595c...d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef). That increment has 14 files:

1. `README.md`, `PROOF.md` — statement, arithmetic mechanism and limits.
2. `fixed_prime_math.py`, `expected.json` — exact recomputation and pinned result.
3. `verify.py`, `SOURCE.json`, `MANIFEST.json` — source pins, integrity checks and replay.
4. `Prime.lean`, `lakefile.toml`, `lean-toolchain` — kernel-checked prime/density facts only.
5. `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`, `requirements.txt` — provenance, license and dependencies.
6. `.github/workflows/multicut-fixed-prime.yml` — replay and Lean job.

## Reproduction and verification

From the repository root (Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.14.0, GNU-compatible C++17 and Boost headers):

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/multicut-kernel-condensation/requirements.txt
python3 -B research/multicut-kernel-condensation-fixed-prime/verify.py --output /tmp/multicut-fixed-prime
```

The final head SHA `d2c63486d895860a65f25b80a51f4b2ec4f3c6ef` has successful Actions runs: [full repository workflow](https://github.com/sennemmi/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38016270013) (52/52: all 16 `make verify-*` groups across Python 3.11/3.13/3.14, ranked-pair finite replay and three formal jobs) and [fixed-prime replay workflow](https://github.com/sennemmi/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38016270114) (exact replay plus Lean prime/density kernel check). The Lean job does not prove the multiplication theorem. The `gh pr checks` view does not expose a PR check suite for these push runs; the linked Actions records identify the exact SHA directly.

## Closeout status and scope

This is a conditional finite research result, not an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or a practical runtime claim. It inherits #259/#249's all-size compiler, common weighted chart, restored-row, routing, prime-supply, precision/recovery, complex-correctness and analytic-reduction obligations; these interfaces are not proved by this certificate. The parent #259 remains open and unmerged, so this PR remains Draft. No further maintenance or record claim is planned.

The later comparable [PR #263](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/263) reports `355516119100349/(5·10^17)`, exceeds this result by `2848213271121654119/10^27`, and has 52/52 full repository jobs passing on head `87129308f762f86a9d8e9a60f5d6c8ef23ce1f6e`, along with its terminal and recycled-bit workflows. Its author reports a physically checked retiming of 25 internal ADD gate frames on #259's construction. This PR therefore makes no current-frontier claim. PR #262's larger priced target is explicitly marked “not a witness” by its author and leaves the physical placement obligation B1 open; it is not treated as a completed construction. The `7.547361e-4` figure in #256 is a complex-supplier saving, not a final `kappa` value.

The other sennemmi Drafts are being archived with their histories retained: #140 (terminal-elision/shrunk-frame composition; targeted deferred-witness checks failed), #198 (endpoint-frame/leaf bootstrap; full CI failed), #213 (five-level cascade bootstrap; targeted checks passed, root workflow cancelled and inherited full replay remains limited), #230 (plateau retiming; full and targeted workflows passed), #247 (fixed-prime refinement on #244; workflows passed), #253 (fixed-prime refinement on #251; workflows passed), and #257 (eight-level refinement on #254; targeted workflows passed, root workflow cancelled). All depend on unmerged upstream branches; their independent ideas and negative verification results remain in their PR histories. A consolidated public research closeout is supplied with this task.

title: Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time (B1 open, not a witness)
body:
# Conditional κ = 8.339545889388e-4 on #233's row: the bit word's own retained ledger banked a second time, which spends the whole complex branch

**κ = 416977294469409/500000000000000000 = 8.339545889388e-4**, and `binding = complex` for the
first time on this ladder: **+14.5981% over #246's rung** (`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` =
7.277211262868e-4). The schedule those absorptions need is **measured here, not merely owed**: the
retained bit row is re-derived, every family's two readings of the bank criterion are applied, the
leader's three absorptions are applied by hand -- a whole family out, the padding per bank drawn
out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the bank count -- and the point is priced
through the unchanged 47-constraint assembly. The claim is still a **priced target on a scheduled
row**: conditional on C1-C7 and on #219's inherited R1-R4, whose PRs are unmerged and pinned by
digest. Not a witness.

Package: `research/complex-bank-run3/`, self-contained on the branch, extended in place. It vendors
#219's rung-1 package byte-identically under `references/pr219-run1/` and #207's frontier
certificate and #233's row, and pins **66 files by sha256**.

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3 && python3 -B verify.py
```

## Result

The ladder has been **bit-bound since rung 2**, and the leaf that bounded it had been treated as a
constant of #219's word. It is not one: the rung-1 retained row is a ledger with thirteen more
bankable families in it, and every absorption lowers the retained mass, so the leaf itself moves.
The rank-3 rung on #233's row (`bitrung.py`'s baseline, and #246's point):

| rung on #233's row (head `109a857`, pinned by digest) | value |
| --- | --- |
| banks | 4,086 (1,362 per copy), 22 rank-3 blocks × 3 registers, **padding 0** |
| retained coarse saving | `417325324839139/5·10^17` = 8.346506496783e-4, the next 10⁻¹⁸ grid point up excluded |
| budget | the bit leaf `7.282510899902e-4` — **bit-bound**, so the complex supplier did not bind |
| **κ** | **`1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4**, `binding = bit` |

The screen: thirteen of the retained row's 21 families can leave into whole width-72 banks or into
the padded schedule a bank admits, so every rung of up to three of them is priced (13 + 78 + 286 =
**377 rungs**), by the vendored interval-moment engine. The leading rows, exactly as `bitrung.json`
records them (the gains are the recorded kappas divided by the rank-3 rung's):

| absorb | banks | retained W | bit leaf | kappa | binding | gain over #246 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| rank 20 | 5,280 of 3 blocks + 12 registers | 45,006 | 7.957727174054441e-4 | `397569983356707/500000000000000000` = 7.95139966713414e-4 | bit | +9.2644% |
| ranks 4, 20 | 6,878 (rank 4 exactly filled, rank 20 as above) | 43,408 | 8.337650404202950e-4 | `104133806924797/125000000000000000` = 8.33070455398376e-4 | bit | +14.4766% |
| rank 21 alone | 15,018 of 3 blocks + 9 registers | 35,268 | 9.319873169802724e-4 | `416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4 | **complex** | +14.5981% |
| **ranks 7, 8, 20 (the leader)** | **7,342** (1,224 of 10 blocks + 2 registers; 838 of 9, exact; 5,280 of 3 + 12) | **42,944** | **8.349765438523530e-4** | **`416977294469409/500000000000000000` = 8.339545889388e-4** | **complex** | **+14.5981%** |

| against | value | gain | asserted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the rung below, on the same row (#246) | `1819302815717/25·10¹⁴` = 7.277211262868e-4 | **+14.5981%** | asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| the frontier this package prices against (#207) | `1366380910073/2·10¹⁵` = 6.831904550365e-4 | +22.07% | the comparison is asserted, by `verify.py`, offline |
| this package's previous top (the padded rung 4) | `711599961413937/10^18` = 7.11599961413937e-4 | +17.19% | stated |
| the record published on `main` (#186) | `330942774629799/5·10¹⁷` = 6.61885549259598e-4 | +26.0% | stated, dated |
| the highest other open claim at the time of writing (#257) | 7.104652045e-4 | +17.4% | stated, dated |

The two *asserted* rows cannot drift: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives both numbers from the
pinned bytes and asserts the comparisons (there, the two gains are exact quotients of recorded
values). The three *stated* rows are dated observations of this package and of the queue, and are
labelled as such.

## Why the bit leaf was the lever, and what the criterion is

#219's rung 1 absorbs the rank-22 family of the PR200/PR205 packed bit word into 6,116 whole
width-72 banks and leaves a retained row of `W = 50,286` roles, rank mass 3,614,784, deficit 5,808
and 857,622 children over 21 ranks, whose certified paid saving -- bootstrapped through #185's
three-level chain -- is the leaf `7.282510899902e-4`. Every reading of this package so far priced
*that* row as it stands, which is why the earlier sections concluded that `7.5e-4`, `8e-4` and
`1e-3` were out of reach on this word. `bitrung.py` prices the row one rung further: a second family
can leave the **same** retained ledger into whole banks, the way the rank-22 bin did, and the leaf
rises by **+14.6550%** to `8.349765438523530e-4`.

The criterion is rung 1's, restated on the retained row and read two ways, because the two readings
are not the same rung:

* the **volume** reading: the family's own volume is a whole number of width-72 banks,
  `72 | rank * n_rank`;
* the **padded** reading: what a bank can actually host when the rank does not divide the width --
  `capacity = 72 // rank` blocks of the family plus `72 mod rank` registers of padding in every
  bank, so it needs saturation (`capacity | n_rank`) and a retained bin that can supply the padding.
  This is T1's padded schedule, one word over, and the module checks rather than asserts that each
  padded step needs its own bank count: rank 7's volume reading prices 1,190 banks where its
  schedule needs 1,224 (`1,190 × 10 = 11,900 < 12,240` items), and rank 20's prices 4,400 where its
  schedule needs 5,280 (`4,400 × 3 = 13,200 < 15,840` items).  The rung prices the schedule, not the
  accounting.

The schedule keeps the retained row's identity: `W = 42,944`, rank mass 3,086,160, deficit 5,808,
756,192 children over 18 families, the stock dropping by exactly the 7,342 banks, and **65,808
registers of padding in all** drawn as a partial removal from the singleton bin -- exactly what T1
does on the complex side.

**The binding side changes here, and that is the result.** The leader's leaf sits *above* the
complex branch it has to clear (the rung reaches `1.000390455784346` of that branch), so the budget
is the branch `417325324839138999999999582174675160861/5·10⁴¹` and the kappa is
`416977294469409/500000000000000000`, the last `10⁻¹⁸` grid point at or below #233's row's complex
ceiling `417325324839139/500417325324839139`. So the wall moves rather than disappears: every
further bit rung is capped by the complex side, and the next increment is the complex supplier
again -- or a new bit word that lifts the leaf without spending the branch.

## The plateau: 108 rungs, one point

**108 of the 377 screened rungs** price `416977294469409/500000000000000000`, because once a rung's
bit leaf clears the complex branch the budget is the branch and every such rung lands on the same
point: the screen is not choosing among them, the cap is. The point therefore does not depend on
which rung is quoted; only the cheapest bank count does, and the package's own leader rule (highest
kappa, ties broken by the fewest banks, then by the sorted ranks) is why the claimed rung is ranks
7, 8 and 20 at 7,342 banks rather than rank 21 alone (15,018 banks) or ranks 4 and 21 (16,616).
Both sides of the plateau are asserted: every rung that carries the point is complex-bound, and
every bit-bound rung lands strictly below it.

## What proves it

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3
python3 -B verify.py            # check: pins, rebuild, compare with certificate.json, bitrung.json and occurrences-bitrung.json
python3 -B bitrung.py           # the measurement: writes bitrung.json
python3 -B bitinstance.py       # B1: the item maps, bank tables, padding draw and induced ledger
python3 -B importer66.py --self-test   # the harness's own thirteen cases
cd references/pr219-run1 && python3 -B verify.py   # the vendored rung-1 package, in place
```

`verify.py` pins **66 files by sha256** -- the 37 this package owns (bitrung.py, bitinstance.py and
their two artifacts among them, and the ranked heads of #233), the two upstream certificates it is
priced against (#207's frontier and #233's row), the 16 the vendored rung-1 package of #219 carries
and the 11 of the bit drop -- and
rebuilds the whole complex-side ladder (base, rung 2, rungs 3 and 4, both paid moments per rung,
the two 47-constraint assemblies with adjacent-grid rejection, the eligibility and width scans, the
PR208 replica, the padded schedule, the instanced inventories and all three export contracts), then
checks the new rung: `verify.py → check_bit_rung` re-derives the rung-1 retained row **from the
pinned packed certificate with plain integer and `Fraction` arithmetic, no package module and no
engine**, re-checks every family's two readings, applies the leader's three absorptions by hand
(whole family out, the padding per bank out of the singleton bin, the stock falling by exactly the
bank count), re-runs the bootstrap chain and the assembly rule, computes the kappa on the grid
below the bound, asserts the leader's minimality on the plateau and both comparisons above, and
compares the whole measurement with `bitrung.json`. `verify.py -> check_bit_instancing` does the
same for B1: it rebuilds the instancing, recomputes both digests from the addressing rule rather
than trusting them, re-checks the padding as a partial removal from the singleton bin, asserts that
the induced ledger is the row `check_bit_rung` prices, and asserts that the pins still export no
block and no occurrence of these three families. verify.py reproduces #207's, #219's and #224's
published grid points, and the rank-3 rung's own, exactly -- the bit rung's complex branch *is* the
rank-3 rung's recorded coarse saving, which `check_bit_rung` asserts rather than assumes.

The package's own path-filtered workflow (`.github/workflows/complex-bank-ladder.yml`, 3.11, 3.13,
3.14: `verify.py`, the vendored package's self-check, the three contracts' self-tests, then
`git diff --exit-code`) and the repository test module (`tests/test_complex_bank_run3.py`, which now
also asserts this rung's kappa, its complex binding, the leader and the plateau) cover it. The
change extends the package's own files (`bitrung.py`, `bitrung.json`, `verify.py`, `pins.py`,
`run3.py`, `obligations.json`, `README.md`, the regenerated `SOURCE.json` and `certificate.json`) and
the test module; the pinned vendored inputs, the other rungs' artifacts and the three export
contracts are untouched.

## Status

* **B1 is `INVENTORY_INSTANCED_AT_SCHEDULE_LEVEL`** (`obligations.json`), the bit side's second
  absorption: its schedule half is **instanced** -- `bitinstance.py` gives every one of the 35,622
  items of ranks 7, 8 and 20 a bank, a block and an offset, fills every bank exactly with the
  family's blocks plus the padding it draws, names the 65,808 registers of that padding item by
  item out of the retained singleton bin (digested, `1828/10481` of the bin), digests each family's
  bank table, and re-derives the ledger the absorptions induce (stock 50,286 -> 42,944, rank mass
  3,614,784 -> 3,086,160, 857,622 children -> 756,192 over 18 families) from the pinned packed
  certificate. Its **provenance half is open**, and machine-read rather than asserted: the pins
  carry no key containing `block` or `occurrence` for this word -- the packed certificate's single
  `assign` key is its own rejection control -- so each of those 35,622 items has an address and no
  identity, and the shape owed is #219's rank-22 inventory, key for key (`H`, `H_center`, `Y`,
  `src`). The no-other-bin-moves proof is owed with it.
* **R1-R4** (inherited verbatim from #219) and **C1-C7** are unchanged: the normalizer, the formal
  columns, the charts and prime witnesses, the envelope parity and each child's frame/chain
  provenance. The absorbed families need the new residual types the suppliers' proofs reserve,
  exactly as the complex rungs do, and the rows are pinned by digest to unmerged branches.
* No witness, no completed finite witness, no unconditional multiplication theorem, no practical
  multiplier, and no Lean/kernel certificate is claimed -- here or anywhere in this ladder.

## Scope and limits

* The measurement is over the retained bit ledger of #219's rung-1 word at width 72, and over
  rungs of up to three families. Longer rungs are not screened; on this cap they cannot change the
  point, but that is not measured.
* The whole-bank volume condition is necessary and is what the built rungs use; it is not
  sufficient, which is exactly why the padded schedule exists and why the module records where the
  volume-criterion bank count fails to host its own items.
* A moved branch fails `check_manifest` closed and the measurement must be re-taken: the head of
  #233's row is pinned by digest.
* Nothing here bounds any other bit or complex lever: a different word, width or frame layout is
  not priced.

## Attribution and provenance

Apache-2.0. The vendored inputs -- #219's rung-1 package, #207's frontier certificate and #233's row
certificate plus its earlier heads -- are retained byte-identically with their notices and credits
(`NOTICE.md`, `SOURCE.json`); **#233's contribution (chafreaky) is the row this result is priced
on** and is credited as such, and #233's source-assisted row and #246's rank-3 rung are what make
the complex branch the productive side at this point. Rung 2 and the ceiling argument are #224's,
the ladder and its replica convention are #208's, the bank proof and the engine chain are
#200/#205/#206/#197's (Chafik Boukhalfa and the #197/#205 line), #184/#168-v4's (icekylinx,
eumemic), #183's and #193's, and #185's bootstrap chain is what the bit leaf is read through;
nothing is re-implemented or restated as new. Prepared by Maxime Fleury with Codebuff assistance.

**Supersedes #246**, which carries the same package without the bit-side rung.

title: Conditional κ = 7.11032238200698e-4: concave-descent frame retiming of 25 gates on #259's multi-cut condensation
body:
Conditional κ = `355516119100349/(5·10^17)` = **7.11032238200698e-4**, +2.85 × 10⁻⁹ over [#259](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/259) (7.11029386054035e-4) and above #261's fixed-prime refinement of #259 (7.110293899874e-4). Stacked on #259's unmerged `main7` branch at `a53ec0c`.

**Full replay: PASS.** `verify.py --output /tmp/multicut-descent-replay` on the committed package regenerated the #249 baseline from source, ran the transform, the new stage and all seven native checkers, and matched every pinned receipt: `PASS: kappa = 0.000711032238200698`, certificate status `PASS_ALL_SEVEN_NATIVE_CHECKERS_AND_PINNED_RECEIPTS`, `new_record_sha256 = 80af525cfdc547090015dc9ab1eaf14fdffe5cacb5b9d0efcb05a4f908e2cc6d` (macOS/clang + libc++; the `stable_sort` fix makes the transcript identical under libstdc++).

## Change

One additional stage, `code/descent_retiming.py`, runs between #259's `cohort-transform` and its seven native checkers. It reassigns the frames of twenty-five internal `forward_gate` ADDs (frozen in `inputs/descent-selection.json` with explicit rational bases, bound by ADD ordinal, scalar content and old-basis equality) found by local descent on the concave paid-rank objective Σ r·ln(120/r). The local paid histogram changes by {2: −2, 4: +24, 5: −48, 6: +25, 11: −1, 13: +2, 17: −1}: one local recursive call disappears at unchanged rank mass 432,833. Normalized retained profile: stock 173,435, 3,956,800 calls (was 3,956,840), rank mass 20,777,000, deficit unchanged. Banks, charts, entrances, prefix kernels, the scalar word and every endpoint are unchanged. The twenty-five registers are disjoint from all 518 pivots and their donors, so the moves are the same ones as in #260 (on #251) and #258 (on #254).

Why these 25 and no more: for a register window (prev, cur, next) the objective is concave in dim(cur), so each gate is optimal at the minimal frame (join of the operands' previous frames and their integer source spans) or the maximal one (meet of the next frames); on this word 99.7 % of gates have both coincide with the current frame, the fully eager greatest-fixpoint assignment is worse, and run-level block moves are blocked by partner chains or spans.

## Verification

- `descent_retiming.py` rebuilds every MOVE from the retimed gate needs and checks: byte-identical scalar/COPY projection, nested chains, unchanged initial/final frames and COPY lifetimes, nondegenerate endpoint bases, the exact **integer** source span of every non-target operand inside its new frame (recomputed from the actual transcript), the expected histogram delta and unchanged rank mass. It writes `lead/DESCENT-RETIMING.json` (pinned in `expected/`) and folds its delta into the replay receipt, so the native price checker still reconstructs and regresses the #249 baseline exactly.
- All seven native checkers then run on the retimed transcript unchanged: independent chronological legality (`PASS pairs 518 ADD 760393 mass 432833 COPY24`), 911,680 prefix kernel equalities, 518 charts and 3,317,400 bank assignments, 23,627 five-stage columns, exact rational price (baseline `88799023305857/125000000000000000` reproduced; candidate `355516119100349/500000000000000000`; 47 strict constraints; adjacent grid point rejected), finite invoice (stock 867,175, selector bill 626,937,381,600). Receipts re-pinned in `expected/`.
- `cohort-transform.cpp`: `sort` → `stable_sort` for the cut gauges. `std::sort` is unstable, so #259's pinned transcript hash is libstdc++'s tie order and does not reproduce under libc++ (the replay receipt does). The cohort transcript is now pinned as `cohort_record_sha256` and the retimed one as `new_record_sha256` in `RESULT.json`; `verify.py` checks both.

```sh
python3 -m pip install -r research/multicut-kernel-condensation/requirements.txt
python3 research/multicut-kernel-condensation/verify.py --output /tmp/multicut-descent-replay
```

Python 3.11+, SymPy 1.14.0, C++17 GNU-compatible compiler and Boost headers; new output directory outside the package; no network.

## Scope and credits

Exactly #259's hypotheses and conditional interfaces; no unconditional multiplication bound, benchmark or Lean certificate is claimed. #259's own caveat applies: the public eight-stage Python command is not replayed on this modified word; the native checkers are.

Dugongue (#259, #254): the multi-cut kernel condensation, native checkers and packaging; eumemic (#249, #244, #210) and the retained PR234/197/200/193/207/211/216/230/237 lineage. The concave-descent retiming stage, the determinism fix and this package's rebinding were prepared by Rohan Arun with Anthropic Claude assistance.

title: Conditional κ = 7.14026746429965·10⁻⁴ on #249's word: 890 kernel families, #263/#270 retimings, #273's target-prefix squares and 126 cleanup sandwiches (#271), composed (+0.42% over #259; above #271/#275)
body:
# Conditional κ = 7.14026746429965·10⁻⁴ on #249's word: 890 kernel families, #263/#270 retimings, #273's target-prefix squares and 126 cleanup sandwiches (#271), composed (+0.42% over #259; above #271/#275)

One self-contained package, `research/multicut-kernel-composition/` (renamed from the first version of this PR), with its own workflow. No existing file is changed.

**κ = 142805349285993/(2·10¹⁷) = 7.14026746429965·10⁻⁴** on the pinned #249 word: +0.4216% over #259, +0.0510% over #271's 7.13662156·10⁻⁴ (99 sandwiches on #272) and +0.0472% over #275's 7.13690108·10⁻⁴, the best rungs on this word before it. Before the sandwich stage, with #259's seven native checkers alone: κ = 7.12005174354669·10⁻⁴ (+5.6·10⁻⁸ over #273). **#276's new bit word (gen4, 7.2287·10⁻⁴) stands above every rung on #249's word, this one included**; the levers composed here will have to be re-derived on that word.

## Result

| stage (each on the previous word) | families / entrance rank | normalized stock W | κ |
|---|---|---|---|
| #259 | 518 / 1,344 | 173,435 | 7.11029386054035·10⁻⁴ |
| kernel families: early-cut twins, headroom, 54 shared-donor families | **890 / 1,719** | 173,310 | 7.11462218·10⁻⁴ |
| + #263's 25 descent gates + #270's 29 plateau blocks | 890 / 1,719 | 173,310 | 7.11482139228173·10⁻⁴ |
| + #273's 209 target-prefix squares (native stage) — seven native checkers' word | 890 / 1,719 | 173,310 | **7.12005174354669·10⁻⁴** |
| + 126 cleanup sandwiches (#271), after swapping the pivot role in 83 pair families | 890 / 1,719 | **172,470** | **7.14026746429965·10⁻⁴** |

Four levers by five authors on one transcript. Three rounds of kernel families at #259's earliest cut (record 676,559, the last initial compensation read): **333 twin pairs** disjoint from #259's helpers (319 on lines eᵢ − eⱼ, admitted by #259's generic chart audit and excluded by #254's `norm == 4` rule), **32 more** from a census of every response class at twelve cuts (nothing at any later cut, no net-positive XOR triple), and **54 shared-donor families** — a new pivot whose twin partner already serves another family as donor, lifted once on a nested entrance chain (the idea of #270's 24 reuse pairs and #267's chronological donor sharing; #259's transform admits it as is, since it only requires pivots to be unique and never donors), with 26 plain pairs dissolved where a shared-donor family is strictly better. Then **#263's 25 descent gates** and **#270's 29 plateau blocks (57 ADDs)**, both selections rebound to this transcript by #270's scalar-core alignment (every ADD/COPY/ERASE outside the kernel categories identical). Then eumemic's target-prefix compression as rohanarun's native stage (#273, verbatim; its 209 squares rebound by post-cut scalar alignment, recomputing every F₂ dependency from the actual word: +5.2·10⁻⁷), and evmckinney9's cleanup sandwiches (#271): on this word 83 two-member kernel families have the sandwich shape on the member that was not the pivot, so the pivot role is moved there (cost-neutral for the kernel transform: identical histogram, rank, reads and native receipts), which raises the admissible sandwiches from 45 to 128; 126 are retired (the bank re-tiling needs a multiple of three), +2.0·10⁻⁶ — the largest single lever here, and the reason #271's 99 on #272's word was the previous best. Every family, retiming, square and sandwich is admitted by the package's exact pricer on the whole word; the deficit 35,200 per replica is invariant, so the gain is in the log-weighted rank mass (and, for the sandwiches, the stock).

## Argument and checks (PROOF.md)

#259's mechanism untouched: the pivot starts at the common entrance (its initial reads deleted), the donor moves there and absorbs it, the inverse is paid at the full frame; the omitted response cancels against the induced one because the responses coincide. Checked on the native word (sha eaff3c98…, behind sha gates cohort 4458dce8… → descent a6d793d7… → plateau a1cf58b3…): all-column F₂ replay forward and inverse (890 pivots, 60,520 reads removed, 2,286 gates, raw mass 434,177 → 432,458; omitted-Q / omitted-Q⁻¹ controls fail nontrivially), the descent, plateau and target-prefix stages with their audits (operand source spans, added frames with nondegenerate Grams, both all-column replays of the compression with the omitted-setup control), chronological legality (1,903 helpers, 0 owner/donor intersections, 24 COPY/ERASE windows), prefix kernels (4 cuts, 1,566,400 target-kernel equalities), bank review (919 exact charts ≤ 262 factors, 3,317,400 assignments), the 23,627 five-stage F₂ columns, the exact price (47/47 constraints, adjacent grid rejected, pinned baseline regression exact) and the finite invoice. The sandwich word (sha 9556bfe3…) is certified as #271 certifies it, because #259's native bank review and price driver assume every helper ends at the full frame: native legality with the stage's final frames, native prefix and five-stage columns on the new word, exact SymPy endpoint charts (126 rank-3 partial swaps) with the bank re-tiling, the unchanged price engine through #271's histogram wrapper (which first reproduces the native price bit for bit), and the native finite invoice; `RESULT.json` and the certificate carry both κ values.

## Verify

    sudo apt-get install -y g++ libboost-dev
    python -m pip install -r research/multicut-kernel-composition/requirements.txt    # sympy 1.14.0
    python3 -I research/multicut-kernel-composition/verify.py --output /tmp/mkc-replay   # about 4 minutes; fresh directory outside the package

#259's verifier with the stages inserted (02b descent, 02c–02e plateau, 02f target prefix, the seven native checkers, then 09–17 the sandwich stage and its checks), each gated by the sha256 of the transcript it consumes; prints `PASS: kappa = 0.000714026746429965 (seven native checkers alone, before the sandwich stage: 0.000712005174354669)`. Passes locally (macOS/clang) and on Linux/g++ with identical transcript hashes (native word eaff3c98…, sandwich word 9556bfe3…); the workflow runs it on Ubuntu with Python 3.11 and 3.13.

## Scope and limits

* Same conditional status as #249/#254/#259 (finite construction under the retained public all-size hypotheses; no Lean certificate). κ is bit-bound; the complex supplier of this lineage is at 7.5474·10⁻⁴ five-stage (#256, Lean-checked).
* Not composed: #272's frame-filtered collective kernels (925 families), #275's zero-frame target restores, the fixed-prime refinement of #261/#265 (+4·10⁻¹²), the two sandwiches beyond 126 (mod-3 rule). #276's gen4 word is a different bit word; none of these levers has been re-derived on it yet.
* Diff against #259's package (`discovery/README.md`): the frozen selection, the retiming stages and their rebound selections (verbatim from #263 and #270), #273's target-prefix stage (verbatim) with its rebound selection, #271's sandwich mechanism ported as three files, `verify.py` with the stages and sha gates, regenerated receipts, and two platform fixes (`std::stable_sort` on the gauge order — the tie order of `std::sort` differs between libstdc++ and libc++ and changes the transcript's sha256 — and the compiler-dependent memo-cache counter `containment_pairs_checked` dropped from the compared receipt fields). #259's own README/PROOF are kept as `README-PR259.md`, `PROOF-PR259.md`.

## Credits

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0; lineage in `NOTICE.md` and `vendor/UPSTREAM-NOTICE.md`. The mechanism, chart audit, checkers and pricer are Dugongue's (#254, #259; donor sharing #267); the descent retiming stage and its 25 gates, and the native target-prefix stage with its 209 squares, are rohanarun's (#263, #273); the target-prefix compression is eumemic's idea (#268); the plateau retiming stage, the 24 reuse pairs, the two e = 2 planes and the selection rebinding are utcorvusvolat-dotcom's (#270); the cleanup-sandwich rewrite, its endpoint charts, re-tiling and price wrapper are evmckinney9's (#271); the word is eumemic's #249 (on #244/#251, #210's helper, #168's modules) in the five-stage layout of hcg890 (#234) and rohanarun (#237/#209). This package contributes the censuses, the 387 families, the pivot-role swap that exposes the sandwiches, the composition of the four levers in one verifier, the receipts and the discovery scripts.

title: Chronological donor sharing: 545 entrances, kappa = 0.000711074913688782665281379

title: Cancel cleanup sandwiches of 99 helpers on #272: conditional κ = 7.1366215638961e-4
body:
Based on main at `3b6b668`, with #272 (Dugongue) at `4d23d0ee` as the pinned base. It adds `research/cleanup-sandwich-272/` and one workflow; no existing file changes. #272's package is not copied. `verify.py` takes it as `--base`, checks its manifest against `SOURCE.json`, runs #272's own `verify.py` first, and then reuses #272's compiled native checkers. The workflow fetches the pinned commit.

Under the interfaces retained by #272, this package certifies

    T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1 - κ)),   κ = 713662156389609974540991/10^27 = 7.13662156389610e-4

That is +0.223% over #272 (7.12074434532274e-4).

## Change and mathematical scope

**Idea.** Some helpers climb to the full frame only to take part in cleanup. When that part is redundant, the climb can be removed. Here the redundancy is the F2 identity `t += a; a += b; t += a = a += b; t += b`. As a result, 99 helpers in #272's word stop at dimension 4 instead of 24. Each saves two rank-21 climbs, and its banked endpoint shrinks from rank 23 to rank 3.

After #272's first kernel cut, 99 helpers appear in exactly three gates, all in the full-frame cleanup:

    t += a,   a += b,   t += a        (F2)

with t never a control between the first and the last. The rewrite moves `a += b` to the cut. There a and b already sit at frames whose sum is a nondegenerate four-dimensional frame. `t += b` stays at the middle gate's position and frame. Each such helper then has no gate after the cut. Its completed endpoint becomes the rank-3 partial swap D_(P_F − P_S), by the completed-core identity of #186 and `research/community-round8-audit/BANK-SCHEDULE.md`.

| | normalized stock | coarse bit saving | κ |
|---|---|---|---|
| #272 | 519,887 | 712581842140497/10^18 | 712074434532274423885827/10^27 |
| this PR | 517,907 | 714171830081841/10^18 | **713662156389609974540991/10^27** |

- **Histogram:** per helper, two rank-21 steps are removed, and two rank-1 steps and one rank-20 step are added (rank mass −20).
- **Banks:** over #272's 120 replicas, the banks re-tile exactly with 1,980 fewer banks per stage.
- **Re-tiling:** #272's own bank review charges every role as if its chain ended at full, so this package does the re-tiling for the shorter chains and checks it exactly.
- **Binding:** the deficit is unchanged, and the bit supplier still binds.

[PROOF.md](research/cleanup-sandwich-272/PROOF.md) gives the argument and scope.

**Assumptions:** every all-size interface #272 retains (compiler, common weighted chart, restored rows, routing, prime supply, precision and recovery, analytic reduction) stays an assumption.

**Not claimed:** that 99 is the largest such set.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -m pip install sympy==1.14.0
git fetch https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds 4d23d0ee5682c99b792614bae4bc5330da19ff13
git archive 4d23d0ee5682c99b792614bae4bc5330da19ff13 research/filtered-kernel-target120 | tar -x -C /tmp/base272
python3 -B research/cleanup-sandwich-272/verify.py --base /tmp/base272/research/filtered-kernel-target120 \
    --boost-include /usr/include --output /tmp/cleanup-sandwich-272
```

`verify.py` runs these checks in order:

1. Base pins.
2. #272's own full replay.
3. The 99 frozen sandwiches: nondegenerate new frames for 9I − J, and exact rational inclusion of every new connector.
4. The F2 replay of all 20,107 formal source, target and dirty columns, with both omission controls rejected.
5. #272's native legality, prefix-kernel, bank-chart and five-stage-column checkers, unchanged.
6. Rank-3 endpoints with exact charts, and the exact bank re-tiling.

9. Equality with `expected.json`.

- **`make entrance-bank-verify`:** PASS.

title: Audit PR256’s complex program against its pinned Lean proof (no new κ)
body:
PR256's explicit complex program and the corresponding Fourier Lean proof live in separate repositories. This adds a self-contained audit that checks their agreement and retains a separate reproduction of the pinned proof. **No new κ, network, or Fourier exponent is claimed.**

The contribution lives in `research/pr256-fourier-audit/` and adds:

- Exact program, five-stage histogram, rational moment and finite-fill checks, plus agreement with the Lean input and exponent literals.
- Immutable source pins, a source-only proof archive, source-origin ledgers, and the original build/regeneration receipts with compressed logs.
- A Lean reproduction command, eleven audit controls (two positive and nine negative), and a Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 finite-audit workflow.
- An explicit dependency table distinguishing the formal exact-complex WHT/DFT result from the bit-side and implementation obligations still needed for multiplication.

The program is pinned to PR #256 at `db3f75cdc5f03f3131d48fb220f6bf1958404ff3`; the proof is pinned to [wht-power-saving-lean PR #2](https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean/pull/2) at `fd19e46b728faa414cbfbf91b01a6a0b7903375d`. This package can be reviewed before #256 merges. It leaves existing witnesses, selected-result pointers, and source files unchanged.

Credit belongs to Jacob Sussman for the formal framework and checker, Chafik Boukhalfa for the explicit program and stronger instantiation, and the underlying OpenAI/community construction. Original notices are preserved; the added notice credits OpenAI, Doug Colkitt, Rohan Arun, Swapnil Jain, and the other construction contributors. Ryan Shea contributes this separate reproduction and consistency audit, adapted from [the pinned downstream project](https://github.com/shea256/fourier-transform-below-nlogn/tree/a101b363b38e6bf7d309042c94ba5fa18a424fad), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

### Validation

- Offline audit and all eleven controls pass locally on Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14.
- The [new audit workflow passed on Ubuntu for all three Python versions](https://github.com/shea256/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38023387048).
- Separate checkout comparisons match all 20 PR256 package files and 456 proof-source files. All 91 OpenAI origin files were fetched again from the pinned revision and match.
- The retained historical fresh project build passed using the pinned Mathlib cache. The ported wrapper was also rerun successfully against that existing build: both generators, staged scalar targets, combined build, axiom check, and WHT/Fourier comparisons passed. That wrapper rerun is not described as another fresh build.
- `make entrance-bank-verify` passes.
- The [broader Linux regression workflow passed all 52 jobs](https://github.com/shea256/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38023387071), including every `make verify` group on Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 and the existing formal packages. The local macOS `make verify` run stopped at the unchanged skip-suffix producer because Apple clang rejects `-fopenmp`; this platform limitation was not changed as part of the audit. The committed validation note records the earlier submission-time status; these CI results are the completed follow-up.

Receipt validation does not rerun Lean. The new CI runs the finite audit and audit controls; full Lean reproduction is a separate documented command. Our reproduction used the upstream local statement comparator, not the official Linux comparator or a second kernel, and is not independent human mathematical review.

title: Finite assembly, source-basis cost reduction, and E8 verification
body:
This PR contributes constructive finite assembly parameters, a reusable reduction in the bit supplier’s finite overcharge, a parent-contract guard for the hosted bit audit, and faster source-equivalent hashing and scalar replay in the E8 emitter. Earlier bank optimization and verification tools are retained.

Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave an avoidable gap below the balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive theorem and exact verifier that select finite parameters for **every rational target below `min(b,c)/(1+min(b,c))`**, given admitted bit and complex caps and the retained conditional interfaces.

The [new package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier) chooses strictly positive backoffs, a finite number of bootstrap steps and explicit integer cutoffs. The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md) establishes termination and all 47 retained strict outer inequalities. It also proves maximality on a supplied rational grid, relative to these caps and this assembly family. The ceiling itself is not attained.

### Reusable source-basis finite-cost reduction

The [source-basis package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order) now provides a guarded postprocessor that derives the copied forms from the actual input word. It preserves their order, their literal inverse, the set of source rows entering the full frame, and the surrounding construction. A separate postprocessing stage lets it compose with frozen reset/kernel selections without changing their original hashes or receipts.

| Pinned construction | Complete finite coefficient | Two-level coefficient | Extra local additions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR433 R758 | 223 to 192 bits | 483 to 420 bits | 32 |
| PR438 R747 after resets/kernel | 226 to 193 bits | 488 to 423 bits | 32 |

The added operations are fully charged. The lower cancellation-free prefix dominates that added cost. **Both supplier caps and the multiplication exponent stay unchanged.** This improves a rigorous finite overcharge; it makes no practical runtime or current numerical lead claim. It is not guaranteed to improve every word.

The PR433 five-stage changed-bit run is retained. On [PR438](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/438), pinned at `e3b56de7869f6af88d48ac0ab1d7959c4c9e6176`, all nine stages passed in one 18.49-second run: original construction/reset/kernel checks, the separate basis stage, and unchanged exporter/global/audit/price/combined checks. The new word restores all 987 local and 7,683 global columns, with eight bank controls, four outer controls and all 47 strict inequalities passing. Its κ remains `45340333148791/40000000000000000`.

The candidate has a fresh complete invoice. The baseline cost is reconstructed from its literally replayed word and the unchanged verified geometry/schedule; its full global pipeline was not rerun. Eleven unchanged outputs from the independently completed PR433 complex component are explicitly reused, with source, canonical-word and recipe bindings. No new complex or phase execution is claimed.

The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order/PROOF.md), source bindings, exact executed adapters, original/new words, receipts and stage logs are retained. The self-contained audit independently checks both constructions' literal orientations, copied forms, omission controls, prefix growth and complete invoices. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 75-input package; manifest is `3df3113896b1130f2770f26da08ec7f4b812e822d568cce69b0f75ba7eb2cd17`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/verify.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/test_postprocess.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/postprocess.py original.json candidate.json
```

Three focused test contracts cover both exact reconstructions, input preservation and idempotence, unsafe basis interfaces, and CLI overwrite protection. The output is a candidate: each new word still needs its supplier's complete admission checks. The postprocessor and offline audit are portable. The retained PR438 adapter records the exact executed temporary paths; it is evidence, not a portable CLI. The existing PR433 full replay wrapper has input-only validation, with its original completed scientific run retained separately.

### Preserve the inherited contract in the hosted bit audit

The original [PR442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/442) generator preserves its parent scalar schedule, but its independent bit hosting audit does not enforce that preservation. On the authentic published hosted template, deleting the terminal exchange or zeroing a bridge coefficient is accepted with an unchanged paid profile, although literal F2 replay finds eight or three wrong scalar columns, respectively. **These are deliberately mutated regressions; the actual published construction is not alleged invalid.**

The new [guard and integration patch](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-hosted-bit-contract) enforce the parent schedule, scalar columns, levels, invocation headers and inherited template fields. Only the bit generator's documented hosting changes are permitted. The original ownership/profile audit remains required; the complex side has different permitted edits and is outside this guard's scope.

The positive fixture exactly matches PR442 commit `4e16d001d505d4f21dd2bcfc44591f9be4c279bd` and template payload `dd7833dcaff8c84b258847f4c4d65b6402c702700ae37d2c464083ee37b24126`. One seven-stage, 4.43-second bit-only reconstruction reused an exact completed reset word, then ran the original kernel, exporter, source-span check, global emitter, parent audit, hosted generator and regression probe. The parent kernel's three controls and audit's eight controls passed. No complex, phase, pricing or assembly replay was performed; no new bound is claimed.

Four focused test contracts cover the authentic positive, the two original-audit false negatives with independent scalar replay, sign/level/header/index/field mutations, and a matching invalid parent/child pair. The offline verifier checks the source/Git bindings, payload hashes, logs and receipts, and executes the exact two-line integration patch in memory. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 38-input package, manifest `f15db9c1ae361b6d0b1f230a23cf6da02add4ea70c1e5907c80d42d9301eac57`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-hosted-bit-contract/verify.py
```

### Byte-identical emitter digest caching

The [emitter cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2c47125cbb0619dc63ccdf64c9c583f064240aeb/research/e8-emitter-digest-cache) removes repeated JSON serialization from the pinned [PR447 emitter](https://github.com/rohanarun/integer-mult-bounds/blob/43e5aa3a2fb6701b1facf542f7f3dee0fbb33c3e/research/e8-eleven-hosting-selected/code/emit.py). It encodes each immutable instruction tail once per orientation and each owner descriptor once per call. A minimal integration patch preserves event order, paid-rank increments, ownership assertions and all other emitter checks.

Across **2,742,552 records and 144 calls** from completed PR438 and authentic PR442 bit workloads, every record byte, independent complete digest, event count and local paid profile matches. The exact source-extracted hashing loop measured a median **3.206 seconds before and 0.587 seconds after**, a **5.47x hashing-loop speedup**. Three alternating trials include cache construction. Template loading, geometry checks, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8, not a whole-emitter speedup or a fresh PR447 scientific replay.

The byte-preservation proof covers the pinned event schema and immutable inputs. The portable offline verifier checks source/Git/fixture/receipt bindings, exact patch scope, every record, and two focused contracts for JSON escaping, large integer tails, fresh per-call owners and malformed inputs. The recorded adapter and original notices are retained. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes. Package manifest: `f45b0dd2c710838f4e5df1c1450c444a7235720b286e89ba946612081c5f847f`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-emitter-digest-cache/verify.py
```

Default verification does not rerun the benchmark. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted loop on another machine.

### Stage-local address caching for scalar replay

The [scalar address-cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/e500c9c4217483de882cf06e6e80b25b70ea1ca5/research/e8-scalar-address-cache) removes repeated local-to-global mapper calls from the same pinned PR447 emitter. Its two-line integration patch constructs one address table per local stage, including the private scratch index. All original scalar, dirty-helper, private restoration, stage, terminal and integer bridge controls remain intact.

On two retained local-word workloads, three alternating trials measured **1.736x and 1.730x faster scalar replay**, respectively: **35.984 to 20.728 ms** for the completed PR438 word and **35.774 to 20.676 ms** for the authentic PR442 template's local word. Timing includes address-table construction and the complete extracted scalar-replay section through its 24 bridge-omission controls. Template loading, AST extraction, geometry, hosting, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8; the cache adds O(LOCAL) storage per active stage.

Both versions independently return identical complete values, levels, schedules, stage receipts and controls. The contract checks **648,692 operand mappings**, both reflections, all **11 stages and 9,417 basis columns per workload**, private restoration and all 24 bridge controls. The retained PR438/PR442 local words are used with the pinned eleven-stage recipe; this is not a fresh full PR447 admission. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes, and no whole-emitter speedup is claimed.

The proof states the valid-index and stage-immutability preconditions. The portable offline verifier binds original source/Git/license/fixture/receipt bytes, checks exact patch scope, repeats the complete equivalence contract, and covers address-block boundaries, per-stage cache freshness, invalid operands and omission of the private endpoint. It also reproduces identical combined source when the address and digest patches are applied in either order. Their separately measured speedups must not be multiplied into an overall speedup. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 32-input package, manifest `643da0bb1ae5f1453f0c31574ac78b08ec7c3f9836126a8c4dbdedeef8cf61af`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-scalar-address-cache/verify.py
```

Default validation does not repeat timing or any supplier wrapper. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted section on another machine.

### Finite-assembly worked example

Using the unchanged suppliers from [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned to `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`, the greatest admitted point on a `10^-27` grid is

```
kappa = 280216238064569651155257 / 250000000000000000000000000
      = 0.001120864952258278604621028
```

This is strictly above that source's `0.001120864952258278`, by approximately **6.04621e-19**. The numerical gain is tiny. The reusable parameter theorem and verifier are the main contribution; no new supplier word, practical speedup or global optimality is claimed. Later supplier contributions, including [PR434](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/434), report higher bounds. This pinned example is not a claim to the current numerical lead; the parameter theorem applies to future admitted caps as well.

One clean default replay of the pinned supplier package passed all 13 stages in 6.19 seconds. It regenerated both changed programs, their scalar and ownership checks, moments and finite invoices; the original verifier reused its source-bound Gaussian phase evidence. We did not rerun every Gaussian pair. Actual receipts and all stage logs are retained. The new verifier independently reproduces the original assembly, recomputes both supplier moments and the selected seed with two rational engines, checks the actual 483-bit two-level coefficient against its 512-bit charge, and verifies nine finite bootstrap steps and all 47 strict inequalities. The next grid point, zero eta, zero beta and unit beta are rejected.

Five focused tests cover both binding components, equal caps, 48 cap/target regimes, exact grid endpoints, 100-digit grids, zero-step cases and invalid premises. Ody independently reviewed the proof and code and reran the complete package successfully. All 50 package inputs match manifest `876412045fcd74e87bba4f02704eb312fad77e565e73eecb1c4849e1df92ff8d`. The CLI also exports witnesses whose rational numerators exceed Python’s default decimal conversion limit; an end-to-end 100-digit-grid regression covers this. An integration test connects this offline verifier to the existing Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 test matrix, without a new workflow or executor.

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Add `--output /absolute/path/to/new-result.json` to retain every exact parameter, cutoff and margin. Python 3.11+ and the standard library suffice.

**Current signed, GitHub-verified head:** [`a65780b`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/a65780b0d5664c33da16e704de4d6f228a7b816b). All 60 jobs across five triggered workflows pass on this exact head: [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135907), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203136057), [recycled registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135954), [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135904), and [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135946). The upstream merge preserves all mathematical results and PR contributions; its follow-up refreshes only the mixed-point audit source hash after upstream’s rational-frame optimization. All 11 focused mixed-point/rational-frame tests also pass locally. No new mathematical bound is claimed.

### Earlier contributions retained

- [Exact bank optimizer](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-exact-bank-optimizer): necessary-and-sufficient packing conditions, optimal patterns and minimum replication for the width-73 rank family. An independent exhaustive oracle checks 16,875 inventories.
- [Chart-sensitive dirty-endpoint audit](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-dirty-chart-audit): exact all-address Gaussian checking, including a counterexample invisible at address zero and an admitted positive control. Six focused regressions pass. Its obstruction is scoped to the stated independent-bank interface.
- [E8 retimed component verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-retimed-component-verification): retained emitter, phase, lifetime and finite-accounting evidence for the pinned PR384 complex component.
- [Weighted donor-rank matching](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/gen5b-weighted-matching): the earlier reproducible construction reused by later contributions. Its historical conditional bound is `0.000751075693834608`; later suppliers improve it.

The supplier compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. This is a conditional finite construction, with no unconditional multiplication theorem or new Lean proof.

New parameter selection, source-basis ordering and postprocessor, hosted-bit parent-contract guard, emitter digest and scalar address caching, proofs, tests and evidence integration: George Lydakis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody's independent review. PR447's emitter retains rohanarun's original notices and Codex-assistance attribution. PR442's hosting construction and original audit retain the DaysSky package's original notices and Claude-assistance attribution. PR438's reset/kernel construction remains credited to rohanarun; the kernel method and exact engine retain Chafik Boukhalfa's (chafreaky) attribution. PR433's construction remains credited to icekylinx with OpenAI Codex; its upstream lineage includes Zhihao Chen, ai-nanachi, Dylan Crow, Jacob Sussman and the retained contributors. The unchanged outer engine retains its eumemic/Anthropic Claude, icekylinx, Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures credits. Original notices, licenses, source pins and earlier package attribution are preserved.

title: Conditional κ = 7.22869827347495e-4: a new paired-cube bit word (arc-aware local circuit, centre-sharing pair module) in the five-stage completed banks
body:
**κ = 144573965469499/(2·10¹⁷) = 7.22869827347495e-4**, conditional, with the bit supplier binding.

| compared with | κ | gain |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| highest open claim when I wrote this (#275, 04:17 UTC Oct 10) | 7.13690108083058e-4 | **+1.29%** |
| the source527 package (#210 head), whose machinery this reuses | 7.10069340338651e-4 | +1.80% |

The gain does not come from frame or entrance tuning. It comes from a **new paired-cube bit word (gen4)** whose virtual circuit needs 1,004 fewer
auxiliary roles than PR200's. Here that word is carried through the complete five-stage completed-bank
package.

```sh
cd research/five-stage-gen4-banks
python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt     # sympy==1.14.0
python3 -B verify.py --output /tmp/gen4-five-stage-verification     # about 5 minutes, no network
```

## What changed

There is one new self-contained package, `research/five-stage-gen4-banks/`, plus its own path-filtered
workflow `.github/workflows/five-stage-gen4-banks.yml`, which runs `verify.py` and the regeneration on
Python 3.11 and 3.13. No existing file changes.
It is eumemic's source527 five-stage package (PR234 layout, stage-private width-120 completed banks,
parity fusion, exact geometry, primes, finite bill and outer assembly) with the bit helper replaced.

| one invocation, m = 120 | source527 (#210 head) | **gen4 (this PR)** |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| virtual auxiliary roles | 18,908 (PR200 word) | **17,904** |
| compensated reuse pairs | 1,760 | 1,494 |
| source loans / terminal sinks | 527 / 34 | 0 / 0 |
| independent dirty registers R | 16,587 | **16,410** |
| independent entrances | 2,279 | 2,466 (2,200 rank 20, 266 rank 21) |
| literal stock (60 replicas) | 1,304,935 | 1,283,035 |
| normalized stock / deficit | 260,987 / 52,800 | 256,607 / 52,800 |
| bit coarse saving | 7.10573897320284e-4 | **7.23392746398452e-4** |
| κ | 7.10069340338651e-4 | **7.22869827347495e-4** |

The complex supplier is unchanged: PR234/PR193, coarse 7.47454944651775e-4. The bit side still binds, so
the remaining headroom on this layout is about 3.3%.

## The gen4 bit word

PR168's p = 12 word is kept: the same roots, decoder and partner-pair mixing. Three parts of the circuit
change, and R = c + q − |M| falls from 19,788 (main) or 18,908 (PR200) to 17,904.

| region (additions − carrier arcs) | PR168 L1 | gen4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| per-cube local channels (220 cubes) | 22 each | **16 each** |
| pair module + copied centre (24) | 191 each | **184 each** |
| all-but-one module (132) | 15 each | **12 each** |

1. **Arc-aware local design.** Every plane channel is any recipe tree of support-disjoint additions, not
   only PR144/189/200's edge, face-diagonal and fixed-coordinate options. Each cube uses 29 additions,
   but they create 13 in-place carrier arcs instead of 4: five partner-root arcs from the flip01
   face-diagonal pairs, and eight chain arcs. A CP-SAT model over all 15 recipe trees per plane proves
   that debt 16 per cube is optimal.
2. **Centre-sharing pair module.** The pair module's 56th root is star(2i+bit), the sum of all 55 inputs.
   It costs 10 extra additions on module nodes, replacing a separate 34-addition centre tree.
3. **Re-annealed all-but-one module.** It has 34 additions and 22 arcs.

Its physical layer applies PR200's rules with new producers:

- 1,494 compensated late-read reuse pairs, from a maximum Hopcroft–Karp matching;
- 1,802 descended operation frames: equal-frame groups moved to the join of their inputs or the meet of
  their outputs, accepted only when the five-stage cost falls.

## What `verify.py` checks (9 mandatory stages)

- **virtual:** eumemic's PR168-v4 package checker on the virtual word, unmodified. It covers exact
  frames, the mod-2 decoder, geometry, chains, G-nondegeneracy, the F₂ replay and the ledger recount,
  with all five of its mutation controls rejected. The stage then runs PR200's physical-word proof,
  unmodified and exactly as PR200's `prove.py` runs it:
  - all 1,802 changed frames and 1,494 handoffs;
  - the physical row: phase one, actual operands, nested chains, deficit;
  - the physical word on all 19,930 columns over F₂ and the integer decoder;
  - four adverse controls rejected.
- **raw:** a fresh census of every physical source, internal and target path, with both reflected
  ledgers.
- **bit:** the source527 event emitter and parity fusion (1,510,656 even payload ADDs elided, no MOVE
  merged), then PR234's five-stage global lowering (487,546 paid calls, deficit 4,400). Exact rational
  h=24/m=120 geometry covers two actual ports, two rank-20 entrances and, newly, one rank-21 entrance.
- **scalar:** the source527 scalar program, byte-identical with all its selections empty. It runs on all
  19,930 formal F₂ columns and on the signed integer decoder in both directions. The emitted
  parity-filtered word and its literal inverse are checked independently on every column. Eleven
  actual-context corruptions are rejected; they replace the 25 source527 mutations, whose features gen4
  does not have.
- **primes:** cleared-Gram determinants of all 26,249 consumed bases, at most 118 bits; every residual is
  below 2⁸⁰.
- **banks:** 370 exact charts, with patterns (3⁴⁰) × 399, (4³⁰) × 4,400 and (24⁵) × 167,328. All
  4,923,000 role/replica/stage assignments are enumerated, and exactly the 2,466 rank-5a completions are
  removed.
- **complex, math, finite:** the retained complex supplier, two exact moment engines with the complete
  10⁻¹⁶ fallback (the adjacent bit grid point is rejected), all 47 strict outer inequalities and seven
  margins (the adjacent κ grid point is rejected), and the literal 60-replica finite bill with
  502,915,820,400 bank selector calls.

`gen4bit/producer/regenerate.py` rebuilds the five pinned bit-word files from the generator, the four
p = 12 data files and both producers, byte for byte, in about 2 minutes. This is provenance only:
`verify.py` never runs a producer.

I also replayed the package independently: a fresh copy, run from another directory under a clean
Python 3.12 + sympy 1.14.0 venv, gives the identical certificate.

Outside the package, two read-only audits imported no package code and used their own exact arithmetic
(FLINT and Bareiss). They reproduced:

- all 26,058 frames and the frame legality of every operation, including that labels equal actual values;
- all 1,494 aliases and every target chronology;
- an independent F₂ replay on all 19,930 columns;
- the helper ledger;
- the coarse saving and κ.

## Status

This is a conditional finite construction with the same retained interfaces as #210 and #234:

- the all-size weighted compiler and common ancestor charts;
- restored rows and completed ordinary leaves;
- selectors, exact-tape routing and prime supply;
- precision/recovery and retained complex symbolic correctness;
- analytic transfer.

There is no new Lean and no multiplier benchmark.

## Composes with

None of these is included, and each would re-pin the package's constants:

- the five-stage entrance and retiming work (#249–#270);
- PR210-style source loans;
- terminal sinks;
- more reuse pairs.

The bit word and these mechanisms act on different parts of the ledger.

## Attribution

- The five-stage layout is Henry Grant (hcg890)'s #234 with Jacob Sussman's construction.
- The package machinery is eumemic's source527 package, with OpenAI Codex assistance, rebound to the
  new helper.
- The banks come from Evan McKinney's #197 and Rohan Arun's #237.
- The physical-word classes are Chafik Boukhalfa's #200, vendored unchanged.
- The checker and generator are eumemic's #168, on icekylinx's #144 framework.
- The complex supplier is Avi Eisenberg's #193.
- Every upstream notice and AI-assistance disclosure is retained.

body:
Conditional κ = `724098741932703/10^18` = **7.24098741932703e-4**, +1.23 × 10⁻⁶ (+0.170 %) over [#276](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/276) (7.22869827347495e-4). Stacked on #276's branch at its head; two added stages (880-gate concave-descent retiming, then eumemic's exact F₂ target-prefix compression with 220 square groups found on this word), no change to the gen4 word's banks, entrances or charts. #280 (utcorvusvolat), published while this was being verified, composes the same 880 retimings with 440 early restorations, 60 dirty entrances and the fixed prime at 7.241891e-4; it does not include the target-prefix squares, so the two are complementary.

**Full replay: PASS** on the committed package (all nine stages: virtual, raw, bit, scalar, primes, banks, complex, math, finite; package integrity unchanged; κ = 724098741932703/10^18). The first commit's CI failure was gen4's pre-PR244 `prime_check` rule; PR244's rule (retain determinant obligations for producer frames a retiming removes) is applied.

## Change

**Stage 2 — target-prefix compression (220 squares).** After the retiming, every target reads rank-20 entrance helpers at a 20-dimensional frame; in each of 220 squares of four targets each helper is read by exactly two of the four, so the dependent target's prefix response is the F₂ sum of its three square-mates'. Its 1,100 frame-20 reads are omitted; it receives `t −= p_j` at the zero frame at the cut and `t += p_j` at the square's common 21-dimensional frame at the close (1,320 setup/restore additions): ZERO →(20)→(1)→ 21 becomes ZERO →(21)→ 21, delta {1: −220, 20: −220, 21: +220}. The transform is eumemic's `target_transform.py` from #268 unchanged apart from the stream count; it recomputes every literal dependency from the actual word, rebuilds every MOVE, checks nesting, endpoints, COPY lifetimes, nondegenerate bases and both all-column replays with an omitted-setup control, and rebinds the raw ledger. Downstream scalar/finite constants (626,580 weighted ADDs, coefficient counts, event hash) are updated accordingly.

**Stage 1 — retiming.** 
#276's gen4 pipeline is prepare → physical → parity fusion → lowering: it carries **no frame retiming**. Applying local descent on the concave paid-rank objective Σ r·ln(120/r) (the search behind #263/#273's 25-gate step) to gen4's parity-fused word finds 880 single-gate frame reassignments — exactly PR244's common-delivery-frame retiming, which source527 has had since #244 but gen4 never received: each of gen4's 880 unborrowed source-pair mixes runs at its existing rank-22 common delivery frame, so per pair the paid children of ranks 1, 1, 20, 22 become 21, 21, 2. Local paid histogram delta {1: −1760, 2: +880, 20: −880, 21: +1760, 22: −880}; 880 local recursive calls per invocation disappear at unchanged rank mass 425,742. Five-stage profile: 483,146 calls (was 487,546), rank mass 2,809,600, deficit 4,400 per replica unchanged; per-replica bank call count 480,680 (was 485,080).

`descent_transform.py` consumes the frozen `descent-selection.json` (record bindings, old-basis hashes, explicit rational new bases) and, like PR244's `retiming_transform.py`, rebuilds every MOVE from the selected gate needs and independently checks: the byte-identical scalar/COPY projection, nested chains, fixed source/dirty/target endpoints, unchanged COPY lifetimes, nondegenerate endpoint bases, both reflected annihilator ledgers, the expected histogram delta and rank mass, and the exact **integer** source span of every non-target operand inside its new frame, recomputed from the actual word. `raw_ledger.rebind_descent` recounts the five-stage profile; `bank_check` and `verify.py` require the new counts and κ.

# Conditional κ = 7.24733001963261·10⁻⁴: 695 collective response-kernel entries with per-entry cuts on #276's gen4 word, composed with #279's 880-gate descent retiming (+0.258% over #276, +0.161% over #279)

**κ = 724733001963261/10¹⁸ = 7.24733001963261·10⁻⁴**, the bit side binding (bit coarse 7.25259·10⁻⁴, complex 7.47455·10⁻⁴). This is the standalone construction in #276's own Python pipeline; #283/#284 compose further levers (terminal sinks, transported entrances, early restorations, target squares) in Dugongue's native pipeline and stand above it — the contribution here is the collective families themselves, verified in #276's chain.

## Result

#276 (DreamingOfClouds) introduced the gen4 bit word; none of the entrance levers developed on the #249 word (#254–#275) had been carried to it. This package carries response kernels there, generalised: as a stage of #276's own six-int transcript pipeline, after #279's descent stage (vendored unchanged), 695 entries — 416 twin pairs on lines (e = 1, #254/#268's mechanism), 24 twin pairs entering on their full 16-dimensional first-frame intersection (each worth more than ten line pairs), and 255 multi-donor families (208 quadruples, 47 triples: the pivot's response is the XOR of its donors', all members share a nondegenerate common entrance of dimension 1–18, 59 donors serve several entries along nested chains; #259/#272's collective kernels).

| one invocation, m = 120 | #276 | #279 | this package |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| entrances (ranks) | 2,466 (20, 21) | 2,466 | **3,161** (1 × 476, 2 × 93, 4 × 29, 5–18 × 97, 20 × 2,200, 21 × 266) |
| one-stage paid rank mass | 425,742 | — | **423,714** |
| literal stock, 60 replicas / banks per stage | 1,283,035 / 172,127 | — | **1,277,965 / 171,113** |
| κ | 7.22869827347495·10⁻⁴ | 7.23571590007464·10⁻⁴ | **7.24733001963261·10⁻⁴** |

* **Per-entry cuts.** On gen4 the compensation reads are chronological: each plain dirty helper's zero-frame reads precede its first other use (by at least 41,247 records), so there is no single prefix cut; each entry is cut at the later of its members' last zero-frame reads, bound by content. The twin census of the 13,944 plain helpers finds 1,568 twin classes and 568 pairs with a nondegenerate common line; the collective census enumerates the low-weight F₂ circuits of the 12,352 distinct responses (3,158 triangles, 23,421 quadruples), keeps those with a nondegenerate common entrance in all first frames, prices them under the deficit-fixed ledger (φ(r) = r·ln(120/r); quintuples are never net-positive) and packs them greedily with shared-donor chains. Total entrance rank 2,028.
* **Rewrite** (eumemic's #268 `kernel_transform.py`, generalised): the pivot's compensation reads are deleted (12,520 in all), it enters at E, each donor pays its shear at E after the cut and the inverse at the full frame (2,316 ADDs); one-stage paid rank mass 425,742 → 423,714.

Every #276 literal the rewrite changes is a recomputed pinned value in `expected/kernel-pins.json`, asserted by `pins.pin`; none is dropped (`KERNEL-PROOF.md` lists all of them).
