title: κ = 9.5424356568133e-4: seven-stage E8 suppliers with the complex idle climbs at halving degree two (+2.40 % over #373)
body:
**κ = 95424356568133/10¹⁷ ≈ 9.5424356568133e-4** (conditional). That is +2.40 % over #373 (9.3191395651209e-4), which this PR extends, and +9.00 % over #370.

The PR adds one self-contained package, `research/e8-seven-stage-halving-two/`, with its own workflow. No existing file changes except one `.gitattributes` line.

## Change and mathematical scope

Everything is #373's: #370's E8 bit word and Sussman's E8 complex unit, both unchanged, both in the seven-stage bridged word B₃. There is one change, on the complex side.

**What changes.** #363 split the complex supplier's two longest idle climbs below m/2 (38 → 31 + 7, 32 → 31 + 1). It did this only to meet the half-shrink guard (2 · max child < m) of the inherited complex finite bridge. Here they are left whole. The largest complex child becomes 38 of m = 63, so one level no longer halves the size but two levels do: 63² = 3969 > 2 · 38² = 2888, i.e. **halving degree two**.

| side | layout | max child / m | coarse saving |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| bit (#370 word, #373 checks) | B₃, split | 27 / 56, degree 1 | c = 968197503705007/10¹⁸ |
| complex (Sussman's E8) | B₃, **unsplit** | 38 / 63, **degree 2** | b = 119394377245827/(125·10¹⁵) ≈ **9.55155e-4** (+2.40 % over the split 9.32783e-4) |

The complex side binds. All 47 constraints of `outer.assembly` hold, the complex leaf cap itself is rejected, and the adjacent 10⁻¹⁸ grid point is rejected.

**Why halving degree two is admissible.** The inherited bridge (`FINITE_BRIDGE.txt` §4) uses half-shrink in exactly one place: "The complex child maximum below m/2 gives halving degree 1, while log2 W < 5208 < 10000", inside the external row coefficient A = 10000 + 9909 + 252 = 20161.

With halving degree t, the recursion depth is t·⌈log₂ n⌉ and the row term is t·log₂ W. The generalized guard does three things:
- it computes the least t;
- it charges t times the actual physical stock logarithm: 2·1903 + 9909 + 252 = 13,967 < 20,161, so A and the outer assembly are unchanged;
- it keeps m ≤ 72 (the cover bound) and the completed-child induction gap (49·B > 0).

At t = 1 it is the original guard.

The repository already uses this generalization:
- #144's integration review (`research/pr-review-20261009/check_paired_cube_arithmetic.py`): complex child 60 at m = 72, halving degree 4, row coefficient `4*2571+9909+252`;
- the copied-centers assembly (`copied-centers-assembly.tex`, `research/copied-fixed-reversed/balanced_assembly.py`): degrees 9 and 20, reserve D_j(e) = t_j⌈log₂ e⌉;
- PR234 on the bit side: "The proper child ratio 5/6 requires halving degree four. The one-level weighted recurrence is retained; its histogram is not multiplied by four."

The moment equation is the one-level histogram either way.

**Why not further.** Unsplit complex B₄ prices at 9.5673e-4 but has m = 81 > 72. Unsplit B₅ needs degree 3 and prices lower. The bit side stays split because it does not bind; unsplit at degree 2 it would give 9.9123e-4.

## What is checked

Every step of #373's `verify.sh` runs:
- #370's checks;
- the B₃ formal columns over all 1,585 columns, the PR234 geometry on 7 blocks, width-56 banks with T = 7, and the finite bill at m = 56;
- each with its K = 2 regression against #370.

On the complex side `certify_b3.py` runs the guard three times:
- **B₂**, against #352's pins (degree 1);
- **split B₃**, against #363's pins (degree 1, b₃ = 932783231884153/10¹⁸);
- **unsplit B₃**, against the new `pins-e8-b3h.json`: degree 2, rows 13,967 < 20,161, induction gap 49·B, m ≤ 72.

The circuit binding is unchanged: Sussman's Lean data for `wht_main_block_B2Ge8x` regenerate byte for byte, and his replay accepts at 8762479.

The κ step reproduces #373's κ = 93191395651209/10¹⁷ with the split b₃, then gives 95424356568133/10¹⁷ with the degree-2 b₃.

Provenance: 142 files are identical to #370 (`b7fe9cd`), 4 to #363 (`9df55da`) and 7 to #373 (`3ff87b5`), recorded by git blob ids. The edited files are `portable_complex.py` (halving degree), `certify_b3.py`, `verify.sh`, `provenance.py`, README and NOTICE. The new file is `pins-e8-b3h.json`.

- **Halving degree two on the complex side.** The inherited bridge text states degree 1. Here its row term is charged at degree 2, as in the repository's degree-4 and degree-9/20 precedents above. The precision/recovery interface is inherited at that depth.

title: Conditional κ=0.0011208649522582786: split centres with complete signed admission
body:
This adds complete signed bit admission and refined finite accounting to the two actual constructions in pinned PR433. The resulting **conditional κ is `44834598090331144184841 / (40 × 10²⁴) ≈ 0.0011208649522582786`**. The numerical improvement over the pinned native value is only `24184841 / (40 × 10²⁴)`, approximately `6.04621025 × 10^-19`; the substantive addition is fresh signed-decoder, geometry, primitive-cost and complete-prefix evidence. This is not a new split-centre construction or a highest-current-score claim.

The additive package is `research/e8-split-centres-signed-composition`. Its complex bound is `1183986549206329246771 / 10²⁴`; its bit bound is `561061350132569610283 / (500 × 10²¹)`. **The bit supplier binds.** The final value is recomputed from the two actual emitted programs, without adding independently reported gains.

### Construction and attribution

**icekylinx, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies the split-centre Hamming construction, reversible source-centre bit construction, integration and checks in [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned at `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`. **Zhihao Chen, with OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies PR425's mutable-basis Hamming/common-frame interface and PR386's compressed bit geometry, owner template and accounting. **ai-nanachi, with OpenAI Codex assistance**, supplies the unchanged PR426 R767 word used before the source-centre replacements. Original notices credit its 55 clean-reset helper reuses and 54 frame changes.

Dylan Crow's PR370 bit producer, with Anthropic Claude assistance; Jacob Sussman's E8 family and interchange framework; **eumemic / PR388's signed defining-decoder and complete-prefix work**; and all further inherited contributions retain their original notices. Our package adds source-bound signed admission, fresh compressed geometry, an independent literal complex-primitive audit, corrected signed costs and refined exact arithmetic. It does not claim the two underlying constructions as ours.

The native carrier restores **58 exact Git files**: complete 47-file PR433 and 11-file PR386 source packages, including original manifests, licenses and notices. The only existing published dependency is the frozen ten-file `e8-bit-signed-validation` package. Its relevant signed-source module is adapted explicitly; its unrelated full ancestor chain is not rerun. No previous published tree is edited.

### Fresh finite evidence

The default runs the **unchanged PR433 entry point with `--replay-phases`**, so every selected phase pair is freshly regenerated. It then checks:

- The complex word's **800 scalar columns**, arbitrary dirt, common-frame labels and private cleanup in both orientations; **2918 exact Gaussian phase pairs and 240 endpoint adapters**; eight global coordinate columns, owners, padding and complete invoice. Eight rank-eight and eight rank-one copies replace the earlier centres. The word has **560 helpers**, width **73**, **12,720 live / 13,298 physical slots**, **40,320 helper placements** and rank mass **926,064**.
- An independent interpreter of the serialized complex programs, importing neither the producer nor scalar emitter: **222,204 forward and 222,300 backward real primitive operations**, including **29,252 HALF operations per orientation**. All live endpoints and private zeros pass, and omitting an actual HALF is rejected in each orientation. Primitive costs equal the native paid bill.
- The bit word's **998 local scalar columns**, defining signed integer decoder, literal parity projection, arbitrary helper dirt and chronological signed inverse. Nine retained forms are computed in mutable source rows using **559 basis shears**, then undone after the sequential copies. The complete nine-stage scalar schedule and **7782 columns per replica** are replayed, alongside the emitted template's frame, owner and bank audit.
- **Fresh PR386 geometry**, with **1080 route checks, 240 exact endpoint checks and 121 adverse controls**, matching all mathematical fields of the inherited geometry. The original carried geometry receipt is retained as provenance and is not labeled a fresh regeneration. The bit template has **758 helpers**, width **64**, **eight replicas**, **14,502 live / 14,511 physical slots** and rank mass **925,632**.

The defining decoder satisfies the required integer construction and parity projection; the unsigned XOR word is not presented as an integer-identity certificate. The signed correction needs **8537 weighted additions, including 245 even coefficients**, or **8978 signed unit additions** versus **8292 parity units**. The extra **686 units per local invocation**, totaling **49,392 over 72 invocations**, are charged in the final invoice. The corrected local prefix majorants are **3,885,147 forward and 15,348,968 inverse**. Their counted global majorant and finite coefficient need **223 bits**, within **256**; the two-level coefficient needs **483 bits**, within **512**.

Both suppliers retain rank deficit **2496** and strict degree-two halving. Bit and complex row coefficients **18,355** and **15,445** fit the retained **20,161** reserve. Two rational moment engines include overhead and exclude adjacent root-grid points. The corrected finite coefficient feeds **eight explicit charged continuations and all 47 strict outer inequalities**, with `eta=beta=10^-30` and counted common outer `log2` threshold `14 × 10³⁰`. The adjacent final grid point and complex leaf cap are rejected.

### Scope and reproducibility

All-size weighted compilation and compressed windows, arbitrary correlated-bank substitution, ordinary calls, common prime/chart/precision/tape interfaces, restored rows, setup/recovery, analytic transfer and a dominating stage-specific `C_full` remain conditional. The generalized mutable-source/common-frame proof is the upstream interface; this is not acceptance by older restricted gx/gxcore checks, a Lean proof, an unconditional multiplication theorem or a practical runtime estimate.

The portable verifier validates source inventories before and after replay. `VALIDATION.json` must equal the frozen `EXPECTED.json` exactly. Complete decoded templates, schedules, operators, owners, profiles, costs, inequalities and adverse-control outcomes remain bound. Only named clocks, fresh provenance and compressed cross-hashes are projected or rebound; raw receipts preserve the full provenance. PR433 already binds phase evidence by decoded payload, so this package uses **no gzip-header hook and no native-source mutation**. title: κ = 9.98243154231047e-4: nine-stage complex E8 (≈2^-9.9683; complex +14.036%, bit side pending)
body:
This adds an independently developed, compressed nine-stage complex component using the pinned E8 local word. Its conditional complex coarse saving is **999240641319551 / 10^18**, up **14.0362449479%** from **876248285600677 / 10^18**. This is a component improvement: with the frozen #361 bit supplier, final **kappa remains 804849251275843 / 10^18**.

**Projection in the title:** if a future bit supplier reaches coarse saving `999240640320309 / 10^18`, the existing outer assembly admits `kappa = 998243154231047 / 10^18` (approximately `2^-9.9683211064`, above `2^-10`). This is an arithmetic projection, **not the current combined result**. It requires about **24.0526% more bit-side coarse saving** than frozen #361. With `eta = 10^-12`, `beta = 10^-9`, start `a0 = 384599 / 10^10`, apply `a_(j+1) = (1-c)c + c*a_j` three times using the assumed `c`, and set `q = a3*(1-2*eta)`. The title value is the largest `10^-18` grid point strictly below `(1-eta)*q/(1+q)`; all 47 numerical outer constraints pass and the next grid point fails. The limiting ceiling of this retained outer formula is `b/(1+b) ≈ 0.000998243156187969`; this is not a claim of a globally optimal multiplication exponent.

The construction uses dimension 73, nine local stages, eight replicas, whole-block rank-9 banks with paid rank-1 padding, and two-level halving. The argument and executable evidence explicitly include exact Clifford phases, endpoint translations, final `X_q` and all-live `X_delta(g)` corrections, private work, row allowance and finite-work charges.

Included under `research/nine-stage-complex-e8/`:

- A standalone offline verifier, pinned sources, dependency notices and a construction argument.
- Exact checks for 946 Clifford frames, 3,120 directed transitions, 240 endpoint adapters and all 1,023 dirty input columns.
- A finite template for 72 local invocations and 1,242,936 local events; 14,727 live recursive families and 15,520 physical streams.
- Two independent rational moment calculations that admit the stated complex saving and reject the next 10^-18 grid point, plus omission controls for phases, padding, bridges and terminal exchanges.
- Fresh validation receipts in `research/nine-stage-complex-e8-validation/`.

Reproduce with Python 3.11+ and the standard library:

```sh
make complex-nine-verify
# Or choose a work directory that does not yet exist:
python3 -B research/nine-stage-complex-e8/verify.py --work /tmp/nine-stage-e8-check
```

All eight component reconstruction stages passed from the submitted source manifest. title: Conditional κ = 9.5464544449649·10⁻⁴: Sussman's E8 complex unit re-timed by far piece relocation, in #375's unsplit B₃ (+0.042 % over #375)
body:
**κ = 95464544449649/10¹⁷ ≈ 9.5464544449649e-4** (conditional). That is +0.0421 % over #375 (9.5424356568133e-4) and +0.0262 % over #365's certificate in the same layout (9.54395132518163e-4).

The PR adds one self-contained package, `research/e8-complex-far-retiming/`, with its own workflow. The only change to an existing file is one `.gitattributes` line.

## Change and mathematical scope

**What is new: a re-timed E8 complex unit with the same operator.** Jacob Sussman's `gcert1-e8-r783` is re-timed by four kinds of move:
- single-gate retiming;
- connected-block and sub-block retiming, which generalises #365's move 4;
- in-group piece relocation;
- **far piece relocation** (new): an elementary addition u += c·s moves across gates that neither read nor write u and do not write s, then takes its best frame between its new neighbours. This generalises #365's moves 1–2.

Our greedy search reaches #365's certificate value exactly, then finds 14 more far relocations. The certificate keeps everything in Sussman's format:
- the scalar operator on all 1,023 registers (checked exactly, with every initial value a variable) and the 8 retained totals;
- R = 783, cst = 72, N = 9,039, the ports, start/final frames and the scatter table.

The gates change from 773/1,220 to 775/1,226 (A/B), with two new frames.

| side | supplier | layout | coarse saving |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| complex | **this package's certificate** | B₃ unsplit (#375): m = 63, W = 1,503, deficit 216, max child 38, halving degree 2 | b = 477778832512643/(5·10¹⁷) ≈ 9.55557665e-4 |
| bit | #370's word in #373's B₃ (not binding) | m = 56, W = 1,585, deficit 216 | c = 968197503705007/10¹⁸ |

| complex certificate | B₃ split b | B₃ unsplit b | κ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sussman (#373 / #375) | 9.32783231884153e-4 | 9.55155017966616e-4 | 9.5424356568133e-4 |
| #365 (aliromman) | 9.32928054566567e-4 | 9.55306874505079e-4 | 9.54395132518163e-4 |
| **this PR** | 9.33167230469274e-4 | **9.55557665025286e-4** | **9.5464544449649e-4** |

The complex side binds. All 47 constraints of `outer.assembly` hold, and the adjacent 10⁻¹⁸ κ is rejected.

**What is checked** (standard library only):
- Inputs are pinned by git blob id: Sussman's certificate, `gx.py` and `gxcore.py` (the same bytes as #363/#365/#375), and #370's word (= #373's).
- On both certificates:
  - Sussman's `gx.check1` (E0–E7, including the exact scalar replay) and the `gxcore` mirror;
  - a flipped-sign control, rejected with E5;
  - our source-span rule, with 0 violations.
- The full rational operator identity with the original, and unchanged family data.
- Our own reimplementation of #363's B_K layout rule: nesting, twin gates, stage entries, m − 1 moves, and the exchange identity. B₂ gives Sussman's idle climbs, and B₃ gives #363's (h = 9) and #373's (h = 8).
- Exact b (split and unsplit) and c by both rational engines with the 10⁻¹⁶ fallback, and #315's assembly.
  - Regressions: Sussman's split b = #363's, and the unsplit κ = #375's 95424356568133/10¹⁷.
- Full mode: our search, re-run from Sussman's original, regenerates the shipped certificate byte for byte.

**Searched and not profitable on this unit:**
- a shared-donor kernel through exterior gauges (E7/Q2);
- a lower copy rank for a retained total (no combination of the 8 totals lies in a hyperplane);
- larger K: complex B_K peaks at K = 3, and B₄ has m = 81 > 72.

## Open obligations

- **No Lean proof of B₃** on either side, and **no Lean proof of the new certificate**. `wht_main_block_B2Ge8x` covers Sussman's original in B₂.
- **#375's halving-degree-two guard is admitted as stated there.** Its stock quantities (m, W, R, h, cst) are unchanged.
- **#352/#363's portable complex checks are not re-run on the new certificate.** These cover labels, scalar words and lifetimes, the splice, and the macro-count terms of the finite guard. The gate count changes by +0.4 %.
- **The bit side is #373's claim.** Only c is re-certified, with our own engines. #373's bit-word checks are not re-run.
- Everything #375/#373/#363/#352 admits.
- This is a conditional finite construction, not a formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

## Validation

    bash research/e8-complex-far-retiming/verify.sh --quick /tmp/e8st-q     # ~15 s
    bash research/e8-complex-far-retiming/verify.sh /tmp/e8st-full          # ~1 min, adds the regeneration

The local result (macOS, Python 3.12 venv and 3.14.8) passes both modes from a fresh clone of commit `c248962`, ending with:

```
PASS conditional kappa = 95464544449649/100000000000000000 = 0.00095464544449649 (complex-bound: our E8 certificate in the unsplit B_3 at halving degree two; bit side #370/#373)
   regenerated certificate equals the shipped one (decompressed bytes)
```

The MANIFEST equals `git ls-files` (blob hashes checked). There are no `.log` files, and all files use LF line endings.

## Credits and AI disclosure

- **Jacob Sussman:** the E8 unit, `gx`/`gxcore`, the bridged five-stage word and the stage geometry.
- **aliromman (#365):** the first coupled re-timing of this unit. Our moves generalise its four moves.
- **DaysSky (#363, #373, #375):** B_K, the seven-stage bit construction, and the halving-degree-two layout.
- **utcorvusvolat-dotcom (#370):** the E8 bit word.
- **rohanarun (#374):** the #365 composition in split B₃.
- **Our stage lineage** (#329/#359; #287/#291/#299/#306) and #315's engines (DreamingOfClouds).

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0.


## Lean (added)

The re-timed E8 certificate now has a kernel-checked theorem for the five-stage (B₂) unit, generated with Jacob Sussman's unchanged generators at `9c94857`:

`OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.wht_main_block_B2Ge8FRx : ∃ solve W, WHTProgram solve W ∧ WHTTimeBoundsAt (1 - 8766835/(10:ℝ)^10) W`

The original unit's theorem is at 1 − 8762479/10¹⁰. `lake build` succeeds, `Compare.lean` reports `RESULT: PASS`, and the only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The evidence is in `lean/LEAN-B2-E8FR.txt`. The seven-stage and #377 nine-stage layouts priced in this PR still have no Lean proof.



**Repository CI.** This branch includes PR #318's unchanged three-file joint-dual source-pin repair (certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json, certificates/joint-dual-validation.json, research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json), as #366 and #368 do, so the repository-wide `verify (joint)` job passes. No mathematics is changed by it.

## Change and mathematical scope

jacklightChen's #377 nine-stage complex component uses "the same pinned E8 local word". That is Sussman's `gcert1-e8-r783`, sha256 `4b92f00f…`. The full rational operator on all 1,023 registers, the retained totals, h/v/R/cst/N, the ports, the start/final frames and the scatter are all unchanged. This PR substitutes #378's certificate for Sussman's inside #377's construction. The bit side is unchanged: it is our #382 word.

| --- | --- | ---: |
| complex | #377's nine-stage component (m = 73, W = 14,727, deficit 2,496, max child 48, halving degree 2) with **#378's unit** | b = **999632926176283/10¹⁸** (was 999240641319551/10¹⁸, +3.92285·10⁻⁷) |
| bit | #382 (#370's E8 bit word + our retime + kernel, B₃ unsplit) | c = 251726760077483/(2.5·10¹⁷) ≈ 1.006907e-3 |

**Why it transfers.** #377's paid profile is the sum of three terms (from its `complex_candidate.py`/`global_nine.py`, read as data):
- 72 invocations × the certificate's child histogram, pooled over all blocks;
- 2vT idle advances at the ranks 16, 8, 32, 8, 48, 8, 48, 32, 16;
- 9R rank-1 paddings.

Only the pooled histogram depends on the gate schedule. It changes by {1:+2, 2:+2, 3:+6, 4:−21, 6:+10} per invocation, so the profile changes by 72 times that. Rank mass, W, the deficit and the max child 48 are unchanged. Our `nine.py` rebuilds #377's profile from Sussman's certificate, checks it equals `GLOBAL-REVIEW.json` for every rank, and re-certifies #377's b exactly. It then prices the swapped profile with both rational engines (10⁻¹⁶ fallback, next grid point excluded) and runs PR #315's `outer.assembly` (47 strict constraints, adjacent κ rejected).

**Further moves.** We re-ran our full move family with the χ ledger and price at #377's m = 73: far relocation, single/block/sub-block retiming and in-group pieces. From Sussman's original it converges to exactly #378's certificate, byte for byte. From #378 it finds nothing. The B₃ optimum carries over unchanged.

**Inherited from #377 (its claims, not re-proved here):**
- the m = 73 compressed window lift (beyond #375's m ≤ 72 cover bound) and the arbitrary-bank dirty composition;

None of #377's scripts were run. Only the receipt's `profile`, `m`, `live` and `deficit` are read.

- #377/#352's certificate-specific finite checks: emitter/splice, scalar words and lifetimes, the 946-frame/3,120-transition Clifford frame checks, and the invoice's local terms;

title: Compressed nine-stage E8 windows and whole-block banking for a conditional κ = 9.98243154231047e-4 > 2^-10 bound
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This combines the local E8 bit word from #370 with the nine-stage complex component from #377 and supplies a new compressed nine-stage bit construction. The resulting **conditional** bound is

**κ = 998243154231047 / 10^18 = 9.98243154231047e-4 ≈ 2^-9.9683211064 > 2^-10.**

The excess over `1/1024` is exactly `21680654231047 / 10^18`. This is approximately **24.0286%** above the frozen #361 combined value. The complex supplier now binds; this is no longer the bit-side-pending projection in #377. No claim of priority is made.

### Construction

- Reproduce #370 at `b7fe9cdf2da009c947ff6b334c562bc190b30373`, including its original word, regeneration, independent F₂ checker, official record/formal-column checks, exact geometry, negative controls and regressions. Its original five-stage bit saving alone is insufficient to cross `2^-10` with #377.
- Lift that local word into nine windows in `Q^8 ⊕ (Q^7)^8`, so `m = 64`. Use four data pairs, eight replicas and 7,785 whole-block helper banks, with 15,465 live families and nine reserved private copy slots. Each bank contains eight rank-8 residuals and needs no padding child.
- Defer endpoint completion until the final stage. Exact port isometries align complete frames at every bridge. Reflected calls use the actual reversed record stream and a freshly derived rank-8 COPY; they do not invert erasure.
- Retain #377's exact complex Clifford/Z₄ checks, terminal `X_q` and every-live-family `X_delta(g)` signed phase corrections. Binary matrix equality alone is not used to identify complex operators.

| Quantity | Exact certified value |
| --- | --- |
| New bit coarse saving | `1057833103534317 / 10^18` |
| Complex coarse saving | `999240641319551 / 10^18` |
| Selected capped bit saving | `999240640320309 / 10^18` |
| Final conditional κ after three bootstrap steps | `998243154231047 / 10^18` |

The bit maximum child is `42/64`, so the proof uses and charges **two-level** halving: `2*42² < 64²`. The actual nine-stage payload prefix needs 117 bits; it receives a 192-bit allowance rather than reusing the old five-stage 104-bit guard. The two-level finite coefficient has 269 bits and is charged 512 bits. Its row coefficient is 18,355, below the inherited 20,161 allowance. See `research/e8-bit-complex-nine/PROOF.txt` for the cover-owner, arbitrary-dirty-bank, precision and finite-cost arguments.

## Validation

Run `make e8-bit-complex-nine-verify`, or choose a fresh nonexistent output directory:

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-bit-complex-nine/verify.py --work /tmp/e8-bit-complex-nine-fresh
```

Requirements: Python 3.11+, NumPy, SymPy, mpmath, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers. The standard-header shim permits Clang without changing the pinned upstream sources. The complete source and dependency manifests are checked before rebuilding.

Fresh validation receipts are included in `research/e8-bit-complex-nine-validation/`. They cover the complete #370 and #377 reconstruction followed by the new exact geometry, source-bound emitted program, separate template audit and rational assembly:

- all 120 port routes and 944 exact local frame projectors;
- all 3,289 nested and reflected frame pairs;
- 8,745 independent scalar columns, 62,280 bank assignments and 72 local invocations;
- 1,355,328 emitted local events and the literal child profile;
- 18 omitted-shear controls and eight structural template mutations, plus inherited negative controls;
- two rational moment engines with the `10^-16` fallback, all 47 positive strict outer constraints, and rejection of the adjacent bit-saving and final-κ grid points.

The earlier `make complex-nine-verify` and unchanged `make gen4-bank-verify` passed. The full historical `make verify` stopped on the unchanged pinned base at `verify-strips/skip-suffix`: Apple `clang++` rejects `-fopenmp`. A full historical-suite pass is not claimed.

### Scope and attribution

This remains a **conditional finite construction**, not a new Lean proof of the complete multiplication theorem. The all-size weighted compiler, prime/tape/precision, common-grid/restored-row and analytic-transfer interfaces remain explicit inherited obligations. #370's admission of nine copied totals at `h = 8` is retained. Neither the whole astronomical orthogonal cover nor an independent human review is claimed by these finite checks.

- the scalar/COPY projection is byte-identical, and both reflected annihilator ledgers are rebuilt.

The selection retimes **1,093** ADD gates (PR279: 880), removing **922** local recursive calls (PR279: 880)
at unchanged rank mass 425,742. The five-stage profile has 482,936 calls (PR279: 483,146) and rank mass
2,809,600. Local paid-histogram delta against the parity-fused word:

```
{1: −1784, 2: +855, 3: −5, 4: +29, 5: −65, 6: +2, 7: +70, 8: −33, 9: −35, 10: +59,
 11: +5, 12: +7, 13: −24, 14: −3, 20: −880, 21: +1760, 22: −880}
```

The 880 source-pair retimings of PR279 are all retained; the further changes are on dirty-register chains.
Bit coarse saving 362080158564507/(5·10¹⁷) ≈ 7.24160317129014 × 10⁻⁴ (PR279: 7.24095525220252 × 10⁻⁴);
the adjacent 10⁻¹⁸ grid point is rejected as before.

## How the selection was found

The cost model is exact: along a nested chain a step is paid iff its dimension strictly increases, with
first-order weight r·ln(120/r); total mass per register is fixed by its endpoints, so only the number and
split of steps can change. Three searches were run on the parity-fused word (scripts in `search/`):

1. **Single-gate neighbour moves** (re-use an operand's adjacent frame). Run globally, this reproduces
   PR279's 880 gates exactly and finds nothing else: PR279 is a local optimum for that neighbourhood.
2. **Register block moves.** For one register at a time, a DP over its whole gate sequence chooses
   frames from the partner's adjacent frames, the register's own frames and their joins. The partner's
   cost change is charged inside the DP, and every accepted move is re-checked by exact recount of all
   affected chains.
3. **Raise/lower cascades.** Raise one gate to a later frame and close forward by joins (or lower and
   close backward by meets), accepting only an exact decrease.

All searches converge to the same optimum from independent random orders.

## Scoped negative results

These are reported so others need not repeat them.

**Frame retiming is nearly exhausted for this word.** Forward-minimal frames (joins of operand states
and spans) and backward-maximal frames (meets of future constraints) coincide at most gates, because
dirty registers accumulate binary-tree sums whose spans pin frames from below while shared side roots
and partner carriers pin them from above. A decoupled per-register DP bound suggests +3.35 %, but that
ignores partner coupling; with coupling, three different neighbourhoods all stop at +0.009 %.

**Target and source chains are structurally fixed.** Targets step 0→21→22→23 (or 0→20→21→22→23)
because shared side roots deliver to several targets whose 23-dimensional caps meet in a 22-dimensional
space. Delivering the last share at a target's own cap would need a different delivery order, which
would change the byte-identical scalar program.

**More compensated reuse pairs are impossible in this word.** Removing one dirty register is worth about
60 frame merges (≈ 6–8 × 10⁻⁵ relative each), so this was the most valuable lever examined. All 1,760
rank-21 gauges are eligible recipients, but the maximum matching is 1,494 even **ignoring timing**: the
binding constraint is donor-frame containment. Only 2,420 of 8,829 dead registers end inside any rank-21
gauge frame, and the 20 components of the compatibility graph have Hall deficits summing to exactly 266.
No rank-20 gauge has a single frame-compatible donor. A larger matching therefore needs a different word
(more donors with small final frames), not a different matching or schedule.

## Scope

Unchanged from PR279: conditional on the retained all-size compiler, common weighted chart, restored
rows, selectors, tape routing, prime supply, precision/recovery, complex symbolic correctness and the
analytic reduction. The finite replay is not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.

Prepared with Anthropic Claude assistance (Claude Opus 5.5); Apache-2.0. Builds on PR279 (Rohan Arun),
PR276 (DreamingOfClouds) and every source credited in `NOTICE.md`.

title: Conditional κ = 1.000385913854264·10⁻³: bank padding fused into three new free sink helpers on #390's E8 complex program (+0.0166 % over #390)
body:
## e8-clean-padding: bank padding fused into clean-sink helper climbs on #390's E8 complex program; conditional κ = 1.000385913854264e-3

**κ = 125048239231783/1.25·10¹⁷ ≈ 1.000385913854264 × 10⁻³**, which is +1.65691·10⁻⁷ (+0.0166 %) over #390 (1.000220222889528e-3). It is complex-bound:

- b = 40055507598519/4·10¹⁶ ≈ 1.001387690e-3, up from #390's 1.001221667e-3.
- The bit side is our #382 word (c ≈ 1.006907e-3 > b). #390's larger c gives the same κ.

### What is new
#377's banks pay a separate rank-1 C child on coordinate 72 to complete each width-73 bank; #390 keeps 3,123 per stage.

We fuse that padding into the final climb of a helper in the same bank: (M₁·C_[d]·M₂) ⊗ C₇₂ = (M₁⊗I)(C_[d]⊗C₇₂)(M₂⊗I), so rank d + rank 1 becomes one rank d+1 child. This is legal only if nothing touches the helper afterwards.

- **#352's cleanup bracket rules it out for every helper.** In #378's word all 775 lifting helpers receive x → helper gates, and those can only be undone at FULL, after the final climb.
- **#390's dirty-preconditioned bracket permits it for zero-row sinks.** That bracket is target precancellation y −= B·A⁻¹·h, helper prewhitening h ← A⁻¹h, and FULL repair of N_r·x only. A helper with N_r = 0 is never touched after its final climb.

We search #390's word for **free** sinks: an exact combination of helpers already at the helper's exact frame, applied after its last influence on y. The search finds exactly three: 301, 324 and 387, each with final lift rank 2. For 301 the gates are `h276 += h1021/2; h301 −= h276/2; h276 −= h1021/2` (frame 731), with analogous gates for the other two (frames 744 and 759). They need no climbs and leave the paid local histogram unchanged.

Each invocation then has three rank-2 + rank-1 pairs become rank-3. The 96 fused occurrences per stage sit in 96 distinct ordinary banks of #390's own assignment (routes fix coordinate 72). Profile delta: {1: −864, 2: −864, 3: +864}. Live (58,899), deficit (9,984), max child (48) and halving degree (2) are unchanged.

The 16 additional candidates that need paid donor advances (the same count #390 reports) all lower b, so none is used.

### Checks (`bash research/e8-clean-padding/verify.sh /fresh/dir`; Python 3.11+, stdlib only)
- **Pins:** git-blob pins on #390's `prefix18`, `sink-audit` and `prewhite`, #378's word, Sussman's gx, and #382's word.
- **Words:** Sussman's `gx.check1` (E0–E7, exact scalar) and the gxcore mirror on #390's prefix18 word, on #390's main word (+355/403) and on ours. The x/y operator rows and retained totals of ours equal #378's, and the five sink rows are exactly zero.
- **Regeneration:** the free-sink search over all 773 lifting helpers regenerates exactly our gates.
- **Bracket:** our reimplementation of #390's bracket reproduces #390's `prewhite.json` gate for gate.
- **Local program:** the fused program, in both orientations, is replayed on all 1,023 live columns. The replay checks private work erased, common exact labels, and no event on a fused sink after its padded climb. Five mutation controls are rejected.
- **Price:** #390's b and κ are reproduced from its own emitted program. Ours is priced with both PR #315 engines (adjacent grid point excluded) and PR #315's outer assembly (47 strict constraints).

### Conditions
- **Re-opened, with the replacement argument in PROOF.md:**
  - #352's emitter/validator chronology (#390 had already replaced it);
  - #377's padding as a separate end-of-schedule cover sweep, for 96 banks per stage. This uses the retained arbitrary-dirt invocation property, and the compiler admitting a C child spanning local coordinates plus window coordinate 72.
- **Not re-run:**
  - #390's rank-8 endpoint adapters, Clifford edge audits and finite invoice. We add 9 scalar gates per invocation, the bracket sizes change from 1,550/7,800 to 1,556/7,776, and no new local edge is used;
  - all of #377/#352's retained interfaces;
  - #382's bit admissions.

This is a conditional finite construction, not a formal verification.

### Credits

  - the prefix rewrites;
  - the dirty-preconditioned bracket, which is what makes cleanup-free sinks possible;
  - sinks 355/403;

- **jacklightChen (#377):** the nine-stage component, banks and padding.

- **Jacob Sussman:** the E8 unit and gx/gxcore.

- **PR #315:** the engines and outer assembly.
- **Ours:** #378, #382, and here the fusion, the free-sink search and the checks.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa (chafreaky) with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance.

title: Title: Signed target-prefix cancellation on R781: conditional kappa = 0.001002494659629864
body:
This adds `research/e8-signed-prefix`, an offline, source-bound finite construction with

**kappa = 125311832453733 / 125000000000000000 = 0.001002494659629864.**

Against the frozen PR392 head `ac55c57035c197f744390fe4bc9cf49df1b61816` (0.001000220224856110), this is an increase of **0.22739%**. The snapshot includes PRs through 393. No claim is made against later work.

## New contribution

We extend the positive target-prefix mechanism of PR390 to signed donor coefficients and apply it to PR376's latest R781 complex word, reconstructed from PR378. The selected witness has **25 disjoint pairs: 16 with q=+1 and 9 with q=-1**. It does not claim a shared-donor/fanout gain or an unrelated new algorithm.

At a common initial zero frame, subtract q times the donor target; synthesize the exact difference of the two prefixes using source/write-version/frame tokens; then restore q times the donor at their common recovery frame. The initial donor value and its accumulated prefix cancel identically for arbitrary dirty inputs. All original helper/source frame visits remain, including visits whose scalar delivery cancels. The local paid histogram delta is

```
rank:   1   2   3   4    6   7
calls: -8  -8  -7  -8  -14 +23
```

This preserves rank mass and strictly improves the moment for every exponent between zero and one. It removes 22 child calls per invocation, or 1,584 across the 72-invocation complex assembly. The actual dirty scalar operator, retained totals and helper cleanup are unchanged, so the original literal response K remains valid.

The additional mechanism is **two-sided residual normalization for even or degenerate entrance spaces**. For the actual phase-sensitive chart `T_E`, exact Clifford decomposition gives `F T_E^-1 = L C_(9-dim E) R`, with explicit rank-zero monomial unitaries. Applying `R^-1` before the complete old-response phase and `L^-1` after complete cleanup leaves the data unchanged and exposes the standard coordinate residual. This uses a separately checked block-diagonal dirty endpoint, not just a zero response column, and does not commute adapters through internal gates. **The base is #401's word.** `entrance.py` is our own re-implementation of #401's 26 entrance subspaces (119 gauged pivots, 240 unit shears) on #398's word. It reproduces #401's frozen candidate hash `3b78069c…`.

**We re-synthesise two targets, y₁₇₇ and y₂₂₀.** Each target's B-phase feeds are replaced by another exact rational combination of register values that already exist at frames their registers already hold. These are helper values plus y₁₈₀'s restored prefix, read through a #398-style setup/restore. The new frames form a more unbalanced nested chain:

    y177, y220:  climbs (3, 5) -> (6, 2)      local histogram {2:+2, 3:-2, 5:-2, 6:+2}

Original feed gates become #398's source-touching empty markers, so no helper walk, bank or residual changes.

**Discovery is an exact value-level search** (`search.py`):
- It runs over all 120 targets and enumerates nested frame chains whose climb partition beats the current one under Σ r ln r.
- It runs an exact breakpoint scan over register windows.
- It solves over ℚ with the x-part, the y→y identity and the 119 gauged columns fixed.

It finds 27 improvable targets:
- 25 are #398 donors read by an existing restore; their improvement would need their own destination as donor, which is circular.
- 151/157 need gauged dirt on #401's word.

The only same-frame zero-row sinks (301/324/387) each need exactly a quarter of a #401-gauged register (1018/1019/1020), and the solution is unique. gxcore's sixths rule (E5) rejects the 1/4 gauged dirt that leaves in the sink. title: research: shared-donor chains and overlapping target recovery, conditional kappa = 1.016422320428301e-3
body:
Result

Adds `research/e8-shared-donor-chains` with

**kappa = 1016422320428301 / 10^18 = 0.001016422320428301**, approximately **0.3070561% above #401** at `7844f72c6051a4408284c3092490687061675c1a`.

The snapshot is frozen through #401, including the downloaded #376 head `7aa9d9f0247bb60c0519704bbca18990011e2a37`. This is a comparison against that snapshot, not against later submissions. The changed finite supplier, reserve bridge, exact moments and outer assembly are rebuilt together; independent gains are never added.

## New mechanism: nested shared-donor gauges

#401 required complete role disjointness between response-gauge groups. That restriction is stronger than the algebra needs. If pivots are excluded from every donor set, the entrance matrix still has the form `S = I + N` with `N^2 = 0`, even when donor helpers appear in several groups. Consequently the literal shears commute and the inverse is explicit.

The physical restriction is handled constructively: each reused donor's assigned entrance spaces form a nested chain. The entrance gates are scheduled in increasing dimension, so the actual donor register visits that chain once, with every rank difference and later climb charged. No free joins, frame resets or hidden copies are assumed.

This expands the fixed witness from **119 to 194 pivot helpers**, using **204 donors in 42 groups**, with **36 donors shared by two groups** and **37 distinct entrance spaces**. All **484 literal entrance gates** have unit numerators and denominators 1 or 2. Exact reconstruction checks all 1,021 raw columns, all gate-omission response leaks, and the actual nested paths.

## Additional chronological target recovery

A new recovery uses donor target124 and destination125. If their prefix increments are `u` and `u+v`, respectively, the literal transformation is:

```text
125 -= 124
124 receives u; 125 receives v
125 += 124
```

For arbitrary initial dirty values, the destination ends at `a-b+v+(b+u)=a+u+v`. This pair overlaps an inherited dependency from125 to172. Its setup must occur after the existing zero-frame setups; moving it across that dependency fails a negative control.

The old disjoint-role/sum heuristic is replaced by an exact **chronological 120-column target-matrix identity**, alongside the complete 1,021-column raw equality, both independent symbolic endpoint checks, common-frame checks, private erasure and phase admission. All 52 target shears have identity endpoint in forward and chronological inverse-adjoint orientations. The helper/source cleanup subword is unchanged.

Its paid delta is `{1:+1,3:-1,4:-1,6:+1}`, with unchanged rank mass and one extra scalar gate. The broader native prefix screen found this pair where a prior three-target basis screen required an unavailable compatible third target.

## Incorporated public improvement

From **#376 at7aa9d9f0247bb60c0519704bbca18990011e2a37**, this also takes the single frame change for `target201 += helper491/2`: frame203 of rank8 becomes frame942 of rank7. Structural matching locates it at B1592 in the new word; raw equality and nesting are freshly checked. This contributes `{1:-2,2:+1}` and is credited public work, not our new mechanism.

title: Conditional κ = 1.016526770666368·10⁻³: response-gauge re-pivoting (checker-clean) and padding fusion on #404's shared-donor R781 E8 complex program (+5.71·10⁻⁸ over #406)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/e8-repivot-fusion`, a conditional finite construction with

**κ = 7941615395831/7812500000000000 = 1016526770666368/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.016526770666368 × 10⁻³** (complex-bound).

That is **+1.044502·10⁻⁷ over Dugongue's #404** (1.016422320428301e-3) and +5.71·10⁻⁸ over rohanarun's #406 (1.016469657190768e-3).

| | b (complex coarse) | κ |
|---|---:|---:|
| #404 (control, reproduced from our emission of its word) | 254364121477661453089/2.5·10²³ | 1016422320428301/10¹⁸ |
| ours | 508780574407464422817/5·10²³ ≈ 1.017561149e-3 | 1016526770666368/10¹⁸ |

The bit side is #404's pinned coarse bound, c = 255384852701747/2.5·10¹⁷ ≈ 1.021539e-3 > b, so the complex side binds.

Profile delta vs #404 is {1:−216, 3:+72, 4:+72, 5:−144, 6:+72}. Live is 14,322, m = 73, the deficit is 2,496, and there are 738 banks per stage.

**Base.** We re-implement #404's word from its data: its 194 shared-donor entrance gauges on #398's signed781 word, its 124/125 recovery and #376's frame edit. Both of #404's frozen hashes are reproduced (`65b0f9dd…`, `d18ccdc5…`). Our emission of that word under #390's dirty-preconditioned bracket reproduces #404's 24-digit b and κ exactly. None of #404's scripts were run.

**New: gauge re-pivoting.** A response-gauge plan is a span of relations e_p + Σ c_{p,d} e_d. Choosing a different pivot column for the same span zeroes the same response space, so M = M₃₉₈ · diag(I, I, S′) still holds with all 194 pivot columns zero. The rank is checked exactly, and the operator is checked on all 1,021 columns. Pivot dimensions, the residual inventory and #404's bank patterns are unchanged.

The pivot choice is what fixes denominators and which register carries which gauged dirt. We swap four pivots:
- **555 → 748 (plan 28).** #404's word fails gxcore's sixths rule (E5) at register 947, because 555 has five half-coefficient donors. After the swap every coefficient is an integer.
- **1019 → 958 and 1020 → 1001 (plans 0 and 5).** 1019 and 1020 become donors with coefficients −2, −2.
- **585 → 636 (plan 27).** The inverse column of sink 387 stops meeting a gauged coordinate.

We do not use #404's 124/125 recovery, because it fails gx E4 at target 125. That costs −5.69·10⁻⁸, and it is included in the totals above.

**Padding fusion (our #394/#399), now composable on the response-gauge line.**
- The only same-frame zero-row sinks are 301, 324 and 387. Each needs exactly −1/4 of one helper (1019, 1018 and 1020), and the coefficient is unique: there is no solution without that helper.
- On #401's and #404's gauges, 1019 and 1020 are pivots, so the quarter breaks sixths. That was the blocker we recorded in #402.
- After re-pivoting, a quarter of their even-coefficient dirt stays in sixths, so 301 and 387 are fused.
- 324 is not fused. Its 1018 is the only donor of pivot 941, which leaves nothing to re-pivot. Ungauging 941 needs a 739th bank, and an advanced-donor uncompute prices at −3.1·10⁻⁷.
- We also check the premise of #404's research note on sink isolation: for both fused sinks, a_G = b_G = 0 on all 194 gauges.

**Target re-synthesis (our #402).** y₁₇₇ and y₂₂₀ climb (6, 2) instead of (3, 5). The full raw operator is identical.

**Banks.** The 16 fused occurrences own slot 0 of 16 distinct rank-1-padded banks, with the padding on coordinate 72.

**Retained hypotheses.**
- Inherited from #404/#401, not re-run: two-sided normalisation and entrance-chart phases (same 37 entrance spaces), bank routes and owner injections, the finite invoice, and the bit component via receipts.
- Re-opened:
  - phases of the four re-pivoted entrance tokens;
  - owner placement of the 16 fused slots and the fused final climbs;
  - the 177/220 target edges;
  - the scalar invoice.
- Inherited from #398/#376/#392/#377/#352 as in our earlier packages.

**This is a conditional finite construction, not a theorem or formal verification.**

**Attribution.**
- **Dugongue:** #404 (shared-donor gauges, the base), #401, #398, #390.
- **rohanarun:** #406, #405, #400, #396, #395, #387/#392.
- **applecrusher:** #376 (helper substitutions, frame edit 203 → 942).
- **jacklightChen:** #377.
- **#352:** the local invocation and emitter.

- **DreamingOfClouds:** #315 engines.
- **Ours:** #378, #394/#399, #402, and here the re-pivoting.

The branch also carries PR #318's unchanged three-file joint-dual source-pin repair (certificates/joint-dual-kappa.json, certificates/joint-dual-validation.json, research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json) for repository CI. No mathematics changes.

title: Conditional κ = 1.017776060460931·10⁻³: checker-clean composition of sequential and enlarged entrance gauges with re-pivoting and padding fusion (+1.47·10⁻⁷ over #411; #406/#408–#410 fail gx E4)
body:
Conditional **κ = 1017776060460931/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.017776060460931·10⁻³**. It is complex-bound, with b = 254703245981514431773/2.5·10²³ ≈ 1.018812984e-3, and the bit side is unchanged (c ≈ 1.021539e-3).
- vs eumemic's #410 (1.017562145187818e-3): **+2.139·10⁻⁷**
- vs eumemic's #411 (1.017629458064773e-3, opened while this was being packaged; not composed here): +1.47·10⁻⁷
- vs rohanarun's #409: +5.256·10⁻⁷

## Correctness: #406, #408, #409 and #410 fail Sussman's checkers; this word passes

We re-implemented each word from its published data and checked it against the frozen hashes: #406 `3f67e51a…`, #408 `7a5d0d09…`, #409 `e775f810…`, #410 `5243b69b…`. We also reproduced #408's, #409's and #410's exact b and κ from our own emission, using their own replica counts and bank patterns.

Jacob Sussman's `gx.check1` **and** `gxcore` reject all four words with **E4: a pivot is the target of a gate reading y**. This comes from #404's 124/125 recovery, which all four inherit.

With that recovery removed, `gxcore` still rejects two of them:
- **#409, E5 at register 275** (and at 204 for its group [51] alone). Its own sequential groups [51] and [195] pivot on half-coefficient relations (1010, 910). Their half-unit gauged dirt then meets a /2 gate.
- **#410, E5 at register 947.** This is #404's pivot 555.

We fix both by exact re-pivoting, with the same relation span checked by rank: 1010 → 739 and 910 → 531 in #409's groups, and 555 → 748 as in our #407. The submitted word passes `gx.check1` (E0–E7), `gxcore`, a flipped-sign control and the source-span rule.

## Change and mathematical scope

The word is built on our #407 base: #404's 194 gauges with our four re-pivotings, #376's frame edit and no 124/125 recovery. On top of it:
1. **#410's eight entrance enlargements (eumemic), re-implemented.** Our `enlarge()` regenerates #410's `enlarged205.json` byte-for-byte from #408's selection. The 1020 enlargement is carried by our re-pivoted row of 1001, which has the same relation and roles.
2. **#409's four sequential groups (rohanarun), re-implemented, with groups [51] and [195] re-pivoted.** These give ten promoted pivots and 55 prepended unit shears, and every sequential source is read before any entrance write to it.
3. **Padding fusion of sinks 301/387 (ours).** 1019 and 1020 are even-coefficient donors after re-pivoting, so the −¼ uncomputes stay in sixths.
4. **Our #402 target 177/220 re-synthesis**, relocated as #406 does.

Exact checks:
- The full raw operator and the retained totals equal #398's operator times the literal 555-gate entrance prefix on all 1,021 columns.
- All 204 gauged response columns are zero.
- Both local orientations validate, and five mutation controls are rejected.

Banks use 32 replicas, 2,943 width-73 banks per stage and 1,495 rank-1 paddings less 64 fused. Live stock is 57,207, m = 73, and the deficit is 9,984. On the replica count:
- 64 replicas give exactly the 32-replica value, and 16 give less.
- #408's 205-pivot selection re-optimises the same rank-1 entrances that #409 promotes into, so it is not orthogonal; we keep #409's groups.
- Further rank-1 groups on this word all add rank-1 climbs and lose (−5·10⁻⁷ or worse), which is consistent with #409's negative screen.

Admitted conditions:
- **Inherited and not re-run:** #401/#404/#409/#410 normalisation and phases, routes, the invoice, and the bit component via #404's pinned `RESULT.json`.
- **Re-opened:** phases of the six re-pivoted tokens, the 64 fused slots and climbs, and the 177/220 edges.

This is a conditional finite construction, not a theorem.

## Validation

- Commit `616d9d6` on `research/e8-sequential-enlarged`, branched from our pushed `research/e8-repivot-fusion-404` (#407). It includes rohanarun's #318 three-file joint-dual CI repair, with no mathematics changed.
- From a fresh clone, `bash research/e8-sequential-enlarged/verify.sh --quick` and the full `verify.sh` both exit 0 (full run about 2.5 minutes, Python 3.14, standard library only). They cover the manifest (matches `git ls-files`), git-blob pins of all #390/#398/#401/#404/#408/#409/#410 inputs, our #399, #402 and #407 controls, and `compose410.py` sections A–E, `cxcheck` and the final κ assertion.
- The new workflow is `.github/workflows/e8-sequential-enlarged.yml` (Python 3.12 and 3.14).

## Credits

- **eumemic:** #410 (enlargement) and #408 (205 gauges and 64-replica banks; a control here).
- **rohanarun:** #409 (sequential gauges), #406 (relocation), #405, #403, #400, #396, #395, #392 and #318 (CI repair).
- **Dugongue:** #404, #401, #398 and #390.
- **applecrusher:** #376.
- **jacklightChen:** #377.
- **#352:** local invocation and emitter.
- **Jacob Sussman:** E8 unit, `gx`/`gxcore`.
- **DaysSky** (#363 and later) and **utcorvusvolat-dotcom** (#370): the bit side.
- **DreamingOfClouds:** #315 engines.

All source PRs were read as data only; none of their scripts were run. Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa (chafreaky) with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance. Apache-2.0.

1. **Closure and rank-two gauges (eumemic).**
   - #420's closure gauge 672 → [48] and #421's rank-two gauges 435 → [304,111] and 367 → [259,246], with their relations unchanged (pinned blobs).
   - They are literal unit shears with frame closure. All 215 gauged response columns are zero.
   - The raw operator equals #412's word times the 52-shear prefix on all 1,021 columns.
2. **Fourteen one-dimension entrance enlargements.**
   - Thirteen are #423's (eumemic), including the joint 914/960 → [48,12]. #423's 785 is not a gauge on our word; this is recorded.
   - The fourteenth is ours: 838 [204] → [304,204], from an exact screen of all 819 single enlargements.
   - No scalar instruction changes; the operator is identical on all columns.
   - 29 frames are raised by closure, and reverting any one fails gx E1.
3. **Target-125 prefix re-synthesis (ours).**
   - y125's pre-cut writes are replaced by helper 563/2 @336, 367/2 @904 and −251/2 @724.
   - Only halves of helper rows are used, with no y source, so sixths are preserved.
   - The protected x/y/gauged columns are unchanged.

4. **Price at 64 replicas.** 5,859 banks per stage and live stock 114,171. The 128 fused occurrences sit in distinct rank-1-padded banks. Replica sweep: 16 → 1.018468e-3, 32 → 1.018488e-3, 128 = 64.

- **Search space.** Helper and x sources, delivered at their current or next touch frame, any number of deliveries, up to 4 frame groups, and shift/restore among same-frame sources.
- **Method.** An exact rational solve plus a Hermite-normal-form lattice test (each group's x/gauged total must lie in (1/6)ℤ).
- **Result.** Only (3,4,1) via 311 → 935 and (4,3,1) via 551 → 935 are solvable, and both fail the lattice test. Every source at 935 has x₆ = x₁₂/2, while the total has x₆ = x₁₂ = −½, so the early group carries x₆ = −¼.

- Across all targets, 125 is the only new feasible form, and 144 is the only one blocked solely by sixths.

title: Split centres and source-basis reuse for conditional κ = 0.001120864952258278
body:
This combines a new split-centre complex construction with source-centre reuse on the bit side, in one commit based on main at `12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b`.

Under the retained compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{560432476129139}{500000000000000000}
=0.001120864952258278.
$$

The combined saving is approximately **6.9522% above [#425](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/425)**. The bit supplier binds the new assembly.

## Construction

On the complex side, cancel the coordinate-source contributions that appear with opposite signs in the centre and side decoders before lifting them to address operators. The 112 code-line targets then use eight rank-eight centres; the eight coordinate targets use rank-one identity copies. Their total copied rank remains 72. Removing 112 coordinate-source helpers and eight dedicated full-centre helpers reduces R from 680 to 560. The dirty response is recomputed from the new word, and both orientations include literal source/helper cleanup and exact heterogeneous-centre phases.

On the bit side, start from #426's R767 word. Form its nine retained sums with an invertible basis change on the source rows, copy them sequentially, and apply the literal inverse before continuing. This removes nine helpers. Compose the resulting R758 word with the compressed dimension-64 geometry from #386, replaying the actual reflected copy chronology and all new bank owners. The changed prefix needs 223 bits and is charged at 256 bits; the old 192-bit allowance is not reused.

| Selected supplier | Complex | Bit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ambient dimension | 73 | 64 |
| Auxiliary rows | 560 | 758 |
| Live recursion stock | 12,720 | 14,502 |
| Physical stock | 13,298 | 14,511 |
| Rank deficit | 2,496 | 2,496 |
| Certified coarse saving | 0.001183986549206329 | 0.001122122700265139220566 |

Both exact moments include the retained bad-branch allowance. Six fixed bootstrap levels and all 47 strict outer inequalities give the displayed κ; the next grid point and invalid-parameter controls are rejected. The result is calculated from the two emitted programs, not by adding independently reported gains.

title: Conditional κ = 1.128983115440183e-3: an E8 bit word with 740 helpers under #433's complex supplier
body:
#433 (icekylinx) is bit-bound: its complex supplier has b = 1183986549206329/10¹⁸, and its R758 bit word gives c ≈ 1.122123e-3. This PR replaces the bit word with an E8 bit word with **R = 740 helpers**, in #386's compressed nine-stage layout. Pricing uses #433's own bit engine, finite invoice and six-level tail.

**κ = 1128983115440183/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.128983115440183e-3**, bit-bound. That is **+0.7243 % over #433** (560432476129139/(5·10¹⁷)). It is also above #435 (1.128832830332521e-3, #417's kernel on #433's R758 word) and #434, which were posted while this was being prepared. The kernel of #417/#435 and this word's reuse are different mechanisms; stacking them is not attempted here.

| layout | bit c of this word | best published in that layout | gain |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| compressed nine-stage (#386; used by #425, #431, #433) | 282564789736676592463/(2.5·10²³) ≈ 1.130259e-3 | #433 (R758) | +0.725 % |
| B₄ unsplit (#381) | 1064525457834209/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.064525e-3 | #417 | +1.960 % |

One self-contained package, `research/e8-bit-elimination-reuse/`, with its own workflow, plus one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

### Mechanism

1. **#370's producer with new parameters** (67 of 520 entries changed) gives R = 863.
2. **Elimination reuse of dead helper slots** gives R 863 → 740.
   - A dead helper still holds a leftover x-content, an F₂ sum of source lines.
   - Before a later helper is born at frame F, take an F₂ relation among the leftovers of dead slots inside F. One gate at the join of their frames empties one slot, and the new helper takes it over.

The old coarse matrix-count row estimate would exceed the retained 20,161 allowance. A self-contained elementary orthogonal-cover count fixes this: successively choosing nonzero-norm orthogonal basis vectors gives `|O_m(q)| ≤ 2^m q^(m(m−1)/2) < q^(m(m+1)/2)` for odd q. For m=78, including all 9,609 physical families gives stock below `q^3090`; three-level halving plus the inherited 9,909 and 252 reserves gives **19,431 < 20,161**. Routing-time charges still use m². The inherited row-divisor statement and notices are preserved verbatim.

## Verification

Full Linux reconstruction and macOS quick mode pass, with identical exact geometry, operators, profiles, emitted instruction digest, finite invoices and margins; only timing metadata differs. Repository-native `make verify-joint` passes, including 16 tests.

The wrapper verifies 246 unchanged upstream source files and freshly runs PR444, including the complex phase replay. New checks cover 1,320 port/stage routes, all 9,340 unbanked scalar columns, the signed ten-wire identity, all 24 individually omitted bridge shears, every hosted owner/window/remainder and the complete 1,736,152-instruction digest. The independent audit rejects 22 template corruptions. Both rational moment engines, both finite invoices, six bootstrap levels, 47 strict outer inequalities, adjacent-grid and parameter controls pass. CI runs the full wrapper on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/e8-r740-replica32/parent436/requirements.txt
python -B research/r740-hosted-eleven/verify.py /tmp/r740-eleven-new
```

## Scope and attribution

This retains PR442's conditional idle-data hosting extension and all inherited all-size compiler, correlated dirty-helper, restored-work, common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces. It is not an unconditional multiplication theorem, κ=1 result or new Lean proof.

The extension, elementary row bound and release integration were prepared by chafreaky with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. PR386 geometry/global code, PR436/443 local reconstruction, DaysSky's PR442 hosting (Anthropic Claude assistance), PR444 integration and Henry Grant's PR234 row interface are credited in complete retained notices and exact source pins. Earlier contributors and assistance disclosures remain unchanged.

title: Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension
body:
**Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension, checked on `gx.check1` programs and on #425's mutable-basis word.** This is a research package of statements, proofs and
exact checks. It claims no new κ. It fixes what three formats can and cannot do and shows where the remaining
freedom is.

| | statement | checked on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | a contribution that reaches a register by a drop-free path forces its frame to contain the source label, so lossless x_T → y_S needs orthogonal labels | every gate of the p = 3, p = 10 (#327) and p = 11 (#193) programs: 0 violations in 3.1 M gate checks |
| **B** | k_a + Σ_j rk C_j ≤ m; with corrector rank h − 1, m ≥ 1 + s(h − 1) | rank h − 1 on all families (replayed correctors for the complex programs and #425; in-cap neighbourhoods for the bit and E8 rows); **#425's word has m = 73 = 1 + 9·8, so the bound is attained** |
| **C** | the drops that carry a total to its readers cost at least rk(U(P) × U(Q)) | equality: 360 (p = 10), 440 (p = 11), 72 (#425 centres, 57 gathered sources each); for the E8 bit dual the package computes the bound 72, which equals the copy loss #370 reports (not replayed) |
| clique bound | Σ_K k_T ≤ r on a clique of drop-free pairs | ω = p (bit), 8, 8, 12, 12 (complex, p = 4..7); 20 ports pairwise lossless in the p = 10 program; ω = 8 on E8 |
| E8 labels | the h = 9 labelling of the E8 in-cap graph is unique; no k = 2 labelling in dimension ≤ 17 | exact SAT, with calibrations and a positive control |
| **P** | for fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ (one helper set, same slots, slot-carried pairs spanning) the stage windows are orthogonal, m ≥ s·h, under (P1)–(P2) | computed on the complex #327 and #193 programs only (399/400, 483/484). **Compressed windows circumvent it**: #425 (m = 73 < 81) and, for the bit word, #386 (m = 64; Theorem P is not claimed for ℚ forms). Not a general obstruction |
| **S** | a mutable-basis word with b_x modified sources and b_y read targets is simulated in the immutable-source / no-target-read format with R + b_x + b_y helpers | exact on #425's word: 904 = 680 + 112 + 112 |

**What this means for the swarm.** A–C and the clique bound bound m and the copy rank, the label dimension for a given
in-cap graph, and (through the five-stage ledger D ≤ N_data·k, read from upstream) D. They do **not** bound the
helper count R, nor the idle and stock costs, which is where #425, #433 and #442 gained. A further κ gain in these
formats has to come from R or the stock, or from a new port family whose corrector rank is below h − 1 with a cheap
decoder.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/format-obstructions/requirements.txt    # python-sat 1.9.dev15, networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5
python3 -B research/format-obstructions/verify.py --output /tmp/format-obstructions-out   # about 90 s on 12 cores (15 CPU-minutes), no network
```

## What changed

One new self-contained package, `research/format-obstructions/`, plus its path-filtered workflow. No existing file
changes. Vendored byte for byte (sha256 in `SOURCE.json`): Jacob Sussman's `gx.py`, the p = 11 certificate of #193, the
p = 10 program of #327, #425's `FULL-WORD.json.gz` (regenerated with its own scripts; the sha equals its
`EXPECTED.json`), the cost model of #346 (from #310) and the p = 10 bit histogram of #325. The one local input is the
p = 3 toy program.

## What `verify.py` checks

It verifies the pins, then runs 91 tasks in a process pool and compares every number with `expected.json`:
- `gx.check1` with the exact scalar identity on the three programs, the taint replay of Theorem A at every gate, the
  corrector ranks of Theorem B and the copy bounds of Theorem C;
- the p = 3 toy: split scatter, cst 18 → 16, exhaustive optimum over all cut chains;
- Theorem P (rank of the cross-Gram constraints), the forced-copy count (10 per overlap, exact over all odd a, b) and
  the contamination scan (1,160 candidate directions);
- #425's word: frame and taint replay, exact scalar replay over ℚ, the Theorem S conversion and its replay;
- the pinned pricer on the p = 10 bit histogram (pinned root reproduced; context only);
- the E8 SAT checks: uniqueness at h = 9, k = 2 at r = 16 (255 patterns) and r = 17 (256), all UNSAT.

Negative controls: shifted labels and a corrupted port; a toy cut outside the radical; the immutable/no-target-read
detector flags 1,640 source modifications and 112 target reads on #425's word and 0 on the converted word; omitted K
and omitted compensation rejected; k = 1 at r = 8 UNSAT and r = 9 SAT, h = 8 UNSAT, the k = 2 encoder at r = 18 accepts
the direct sum.

## Verification

- **Replays:** two fresh-copy runs in other working directories (macOS, Python 3.12.14, python-sat 1.9.dev15,
  networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5) pass every check; CI has not been run yet.
- **Independent audit:** Independent read-only audit (separate Claude agent): two blockers found and fixed; re-verified.

## Status, honestly

- **κ:** no new κ.
- **Scope:** Theorems A–C and the clique bound are proved for the frame model of PROOF.md §1, which contains the rules E0–E3
  of `gx.check1` and #425's common-label rule; the correspondence is by reading, with no mechanical proof and no Lean.
- **Layout hypotheses:** (B1)–(B2) of Theorem B and (P1)–(P2) of Theorem P were read against Sussman's
  `Work/Bridge/Net.lean`, `Work/BridgeGeom/Stage.lean` and `Work/BridgeGeom/Net.lean` (f010392c); they are consistent
  with the statements there, but this was read, not formally verified. Two points are open: whether the backward stages
  1 and 3 count as "the same program", and whether the stage-j target frames lie in ι_j(q_S)^⊥. Theorem P holds for
  fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ only; #425's nine-stage windows (m = 73) are outside it.
- **Bit side:** no bit word is replayed. Theorem P (stated for F₂ windows) and the overlap measurements were computed on
  complex programs, and nothing is claimed about Theorem P for ℚ forms such as #386's; the pricing context uses the
  p = 10 bit histogram (the file copied from the `math.json` that #325's verification writes) and is a pricer-model
  output.
- **Theorem S:** a bound on helper count, not on price (the simulation prices 13 % below #425's word under the coarse
  formula). Replayed by the package's detector on #425's word, not by `gx.check1`.
- **E8 labels:** the SAT results are for the full E8 in-cap graph only.

## Attribution

- **Jacob Sussman:** gcert/1, `gx.check1`, the frame lemma, the five-stage layout and the E8 complex unit.
- **jacklightChen (Zhihao Chen):** #425's word and its conjugation semantics; #386.
- **Dylan Crow (utcorvusvolat-dotcom):** #370 (E8 bit word, root coordinates) and the #310 cost model.
- **Louis Harrison:** #346 (the vendored pricer).
- **Avi Eisenberg (ikeboy):** #193. **icekylinx:** #144, #184 and #433. **chafreaky:** #200, #233, #256.
- **eumemic:** #168. **DaysSky:** #162, #352 and #442. **hcg890** and **SovereignSteak:** #234 and the five-stage ledger.

The statements, proofs, checks and packaging were prepared by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via
Claude Code. Every upstream notice is retained; see `NOTICE`.

title: Under review (split-residual interface): cross-copy idle-axis hosting, one residual on two copies of one idle child; computed κ = 0.001330733966732373 not established
body:
Conditional **κ = 1330733966732373/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.330733966732373·10⁻³**, bit-bound, **+5.13 % over #447** (1.265848755025709·10⁻³, complex-bound), +7.53 % over #442 and +17.44 % over #434. Neither local word changes: complex #433 (R = 560, m = 73), bit #434 (R = 747, m = 64). The idle windows are #442's.

## Change

In #442's idle-axis hosting a whole helper residual sits inside the pending coordinates of one data family. Bit residuals have width 8 − e (637 of width 8, 104 of width 7, 6 of width 4) and complex residuals width 9, while the idle children have ranks 7/14/28/42 (bit) and 8/16/32/48 (complex). A rank-7 child cannot hold a width-8 residual, a rank-14 child holds one and wastes six coordinates, and so on: 6,944 of the 45,360 pending bit coordinates per replica and 5,760 of 51,840 complex ones stay idle and are paid as remainder children.

A child acts on every copy (side, port) of its pair, and all copies share the child's window. This package lets a residual lie across the pending sets of **two copies of the same idle child**. With P = P₁ + P₂ the identity D_{P₁}·D_{P₂} = D_P (the parents' D_{P'}·D_{P−P'} = D_P) writes the dirty invocation's factor on the residual as a product of a factor on each family; each is moved to the child exactly as in #442 §2, since the window is a property of the pair; and each child's remainder is exact by #442's fact (b). Every child's capacity, copies × rank, is then a multiple of the residual width, so the remainders almost vanish. A residual never spans two children or two pairs. The route is still an elementary coordinate permutation of the address space; the finite invoice charges one further route factor per helper selector.

The selection is an integer programme over counts n(child, stage, width) on the concatenated tape of each child's copies (maximise Σ ln(m/r) × hosted coordinates, subject to availability and, on the bit side, exact width-64 tiling of the leftover). `SELECTION.json` freezes it; `--discover` recomputes it with scipy.

## Result

| supplier | #442 saving | this saving | live stock | hosted residuals (split) | max child |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit, m = 64, R = 747 | 1.239085·10⁻³ | **1.332507·10⁻³** | 9,457 → 8,592 | 46,160 of 53,784 (12,496) | 24 |
| complex, m = 73, R = 560 | 1.267453·10⁻³ | **1.437532·10⁻³** | 8,400 → 7,680 | 40,320 of 40,320 (13,720) | 48 |

Both rank deficits stay 2496. The bit max child 24 is one partial copy of a rank-28 child; the complex max child 48 is the 133 copies per replica of the rank-48 final children that the complex supply cannot fill (5,040 residuals against 5,760 width-9 slots per replica). Since #447 is complex-bound at 1.267453·10⁻³, the complex component here should also lift #445/#447's eleven-stage bit words; that composition is not claimed.

## Validation

`python3 -B research/cross-copy-hosting/verify.py /absolute/new/output` (Python 3.11+, standard library only; the output directory must not exist). It

1. runs #434's complete verifier from scratch;
2. regenerates both hosted templates from #434's fresh outputs and the frozen selection;
3. runs an independent audit that shares no code with the generators: windows re-derived from each schedule; for every replica and invocation exactly one owner record per helper; every hosted residual has one or two pieces on copies of the child it names, widths summing to the residual width, inside the pending set, pairwise disjoint per (child, copy), inside the window and off the active pair; exact remainder children and bank tilings; profile, live stock and deficit 2496 recomputed; twelve mutation controls rejected (including a split across two children and a split whose widths do not sum to the residual width);
4. prices both suppliers with the two inherited rational moment engines and fresh finite invoices (prefix 226 bits charged 256, two-level coefficient 488 bits charged 512, row coefficient 18,355 < 20,161; complex row coefficient 15,443);
5. runs #434's strict outer assembly: six bootstrap levels and all 47 inequalities, with the next grid point and the zero-η, zero-β and unit-β controls rejected.

Local transcript: `PASS_FULL_CROSS_COPY_HOSTING_COMPOSITION` on macOS (Apple silicon), Python 3.14.3, 5 min 48 s including the full #434 replay; every value equals `EXPECTED.json` and both template hashes match. CI is not claimed before it runs.

## Scope

This is a written finite extension of #442's hosting interface: a helper residual's physical slot may lie in two data families of one idle child. That is the principal new review point; [PROOF.md](research/cross-copy-hosting/PROOF.md) gives the argument from the parents' two facts. #442's own extension (helper residuals on data streams during idle windows) and all inherited interfaces remain assumptions: the all-size compiler, correlated dirty-bank and compressed-window interfaces, restored work, tape/common grid, precision and analytic transfer. The global operator identity is argued and checked combinatorially, not replayed numerically on the address spaces. No Lean proof and no unconditional integer-multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Credits and AI disclosure

Builds on and runs unchanged: #442 (DaysSky, idle-axis hosting; windows and bank tilings reused), #434 (Rohan Arun), #433 (icekylinx), #435/#417 (chafreaky), #426 (ai-nanachi), #425/#386 (Zhihao Chen), #370 (Dylan Crow), Jacob Sussman's E8 unit and interfaces. This branch is #442's branch plus one new directory, `research/cross-copy-hosting/`; no inherited file is changed. The cross-copy selection, generators, audit, assembly and proof note were prepared by higherbeing with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance.
